QC reject % and vehicle rejection % are tracked in aggregate, not yet split by vendor/SKU for a supplier scorecard.
score_4_desc:
10% sampling and 20% rejection threshold applied, segmented by category (FnV vs dry).
Batch/expiry and 70-80% shelf-life checks are enforced.
GRN cannot be posted until the quality team records clearance against the defined inspection procedure.
AQR with fixed sampling/defect cutoffs is completed before unloading starts for 85-95% of lots.
QC reject % and vehicle rejection % are tracked by vendor and SKU, feeding a periodic supplier scorecard.
score_5_desc:
Sampling and rejection norms (10%/20%) are defined per SKU category, digitally logged, with under 2% inspection-error rate.
Monthly trend analysis is done on rejection causes.
GRN approval is system-enforced with zero exceptions, released only on digital quality-team clearance, with a full audit trail of inspector sign-off.
AQR is completed before unloading begins for over 95% of lots with zero exceptions.
QC reject % and vehicle rejection % by vendor and SKU are tracked in real time, driving an automated supplier scorecard used in vendor review.
indicative_scoring_questions:
• What % of inbound lots are sampled for quality check, and is a rejection threshold defined (e.g., 10% sampling / 20% rejection)?
• Is Goods Receipt Note (GRN) approval system-enforced to require quality-team clearance, or can goods be put away before sign-off?
• Is a structured Arrival Quality Report (AQR) completed before unloading begins, and for what % of lots?
• Are Quality Check (QC) reject % and vehicle rejection % tracked by vendor and Stock-Keeping Unit (SKU), feeding a supplier scorecard?
• Is there a defined inspection-error rate or monthly trend analysis on rejection causes?

score_1_desc:
No formal 5S audit.
Audit score under 40% where measured at all.
No physical demarcation of aisles, S&G/packing areas, storage space, buffer-pallet staging, packaging-material storage, or tools/machinery locations - floor markings, if any, are inconsistent or absent.
No designated area/zone name signage, fire extinguisher position signage, or fire exit signage is installed anywhere in the facility.
score_2_desc:
5S introduced in a pilot area only.
Audit score 40-55%.
Floor marking/demarcation done for under 30% of the required zones (aisles, S&G/packing spaces, storage, buffer-pallet staging, packaging material, tools/machinery), and only in the pilot area.
Signage exists for a few zones and fire extinguisher points only, limited to the pilot area; fire exits are marked but not consistently visible or illuminated.
score_3_desc:
Sort/Set/Shine implemented facility-wide.
Audit score 55-70%.
Audits conducted quarterly.
Demarcation in place for 30-60% of required zones - e.g., aisles and storage racking are marked, but S&G/packing space, buffer-pallet staging, packaging-material, and tools/machinery locations are only partially marked.
Designated area signage and fire extinguisher position signage are installed for 30-60% of required zones/points; fire exits are signed and illuminated for the main escape routes only.
score_4_desc:
Standardized across all zones with monthly audits.
Score 70-85%.
Training conducted at least twice a year.
Demarcation covers 60-90% of required zones, including aisles, S&G and packing space boundaries, storage space marking, buffer-pallet staging area, and packaging-material storage, with tools/machinery locations marked but not yet audited on a fixed schedule.
Area signage, fire extinguisher signage, and fire exit signage cover 60-90% of required zones/points/routes, checked alongside the periodic 5S review.
score_5_desc:
5S sustained for over 12 months.
Audit score above 85%.
Daily checks, biannual training, and a documented continuous-improvement (Kaizen) count.
100% of zones demarcated and colour-coded - aisles, S&G and packing spaces, storage space, buffer-pallet staging, packaging-material storage, and tools/machinery locations - with demarcation adherence audited as part of the daily 5S check.
100% of zones carry designated area signage, every fire extinguisher position is signed, and all fire exits/escape routes are signed, illuminated, and unobstructed - verified as part of the daily 5S and safety audit.
indicative_scoring_questions:
• What is the current 5S audit score, and how often are audits conducted?
• What % of required zones (aisles, sorting & grading/packing areas, storage, buffer-pallet staging, packaging-material storage, tools/machinery) are physically demarcated and colour-coded?
• What % of required points/zones carry designated-area, fire-extinguisher, and fire-exit signage?
• How often is 5S training conducted, and is there a documented continuous-improvement (Kaizen) count?
• Has 5S been sustained facility-wide for over 12 months, or is it confined to a pilot area?

score_1_desc:
0-1 of the 5 lean principles (value definition, value stream mapping, flow, pull, continuous improvement) deployed.
No Plan-Do-Check-Act (PDCA) or waste tracking.
Example: crates batched and queued at dock for hours, no flow attempted.
score_2_desc:
2 principles deployed (e.g., value stream mapping started).
PDCA used in under 20% of processes.
Example: value stream map drawn once for inbound dock, never revisited.
score_3_desc:
3 principles deployed.
PDCA embedded in 20-50% of processes.
2-3 of the 8 waste types tracked.
Example: single-piece flow piloted on one packing line, not yet scaled.
score_4_desc:
4 principles deployed with pull/Just-In-Time (JIT) replenishment active.
PDCA in 50-80% of processes.
5-6 of the 8 waste types tracked with quarterly reduction targets.
Example: bin hits reorder point, picker restocks on pull signal, no forecast push.
score_5_desc:
All 5 principles fully embedded.
PDCA in over 80% of processes.
All 8 waste types tracked with measurable year-on-year reduction of over 10%.
Example: single-piece flow standard on packing line, one crate moves at a time, no batching.
indicative_scoring_questions:
• How many of the 5 lean principles (value definition, value stream mapping, flow, pull, continuous improvement) are actively deployed?
• What % of processes have a Plan-Do-Check-Act (PDCA) cycle embedded?
• How many of the 8 lean waste types are tracked, with a measurable year-on-year reduction target?
• Is pull-based/Just-In-Time (JIT) replenishment active (e.g., bin hits reorder point, picker restocks on signal), or is work still forecast-push and batched?

score_1_desc:
No SKU-level classification into ethylene-releasing vs ethylene-sensitive categories.
Releasing SKUs (apples, bananas, tomatoes) stored alongside sensitive SKUs (leafy greens, cucumbers) with no awareness.
No dedicated zoning or minimum separation defined.
Ethylene-driven spoilage not tracked, misattributed to general quality loss.
score_2_desc:
Ethylene classification documented for some SKUs, coverage incomplete.
No physical enforcement, releasing and sensitive SKUs commingled in same zone.
No minimum separation distance defined.
Spoilage not attributed to ethylene exposure.
score_3_desc:
Full SKU-level classification into releasing vs sensitive categories.
Informal separation attempted, no dedicated zoning, occasional commingling during peak inbound.
Minimum separation distance defined but inconsistently followed.
Ethylene-attributable spoilage flagged qualitatively, not measured.
score_4_desc:
Full SKU-level classification maintained, updated as new SKUs onboard.
Dedicated zones assigned for releasing vs sensitive produce, minimum separation enforced.
Occasional commingling during space-constrained peak periods.
Ethylene-attributable spoilage tracked but not yet a formal KPI.
score_5_desc:
Full SKU-level classification, releasing vs sensitive, updated real-time with SKU master.
Physically segregated zones with defined minimum separation, zero commingling incidents.
Zoning enforced through system-directed putaway, no manual override.
Ethylene-cross-contamination spoilage tracked monthly, near-zero.
indicative_scoring_questions:
• Are Stock-Keeping Units (SKUs) classified as ethylene-releasing (e.g., apples, bananas, tomatoes) vs. ethylene-sensitive (e.g., leafy greens, cucumbers), and is this classification complete and kept current?
• Are releasing and sensitive SKUs physically segregated into dedicated zones with a defined minimum separation distance, or do they commingle?
• How many commingling incidents occur, particularly during peak inbound?
• Is ethylene-attributable spoilage tracked as a distinct, measured metric, or lumped into general quality loss?
• Is zoning enforced through system-directed putaway, or is manual override possible?

score_1_desc:
No dedicated Shortage & Loss Prevention (SLP) function or role.
Theft and loss cases not tracked separately from general shrinkage.
No case logging, investigation, or closure process.
No Closed-Circuit Television (CCTV) or access-control used for loss deterrence.
score_2_desc:
SLP responsibility informally assigned to warehouse manager, no dedicated team.
Some theft/loss cases logged, but inconsistently and without investigation.
No defined case-closure process, cases often left open indefinitely.
CCTV installed in under half of high-risk zones, rarely reviewed.
score_3_desc:
Dedicated SLP role exists (part-time or shared), reporting line unclear.
Majority of flagged cases logged and investigated, closure process defined but manual.
CCTV covers high-risk zones (dock, storage, packing), reviewed only after incidents.
Theft/loss rate tracked, trend not yet established.
score_4_desc:
Dedicated SLP function with defined charter and reporting line.
Over 80% of flagged cases investigated and closed with documented outcome.
CCTV plus access-control at all high-risk zones, proactively monitored.
Theft/loss rate tracked monthly, early signs of a declining trend.
score_5_desc:
Dedicated SLP team with clear mandate, embedded in warehouse governance.
100% of flagged cases investigated and closed with documented outcome.
CCTV and access-control across all zones, used proactively for deterrence and investigation.
Theft/loss rate tracked monthly with a sustained declining trend.
indicative_scoring_questions:
• Is there a dedicated Shortage & Loss Prevention (SLP) function or role, and what is its reporting line?
• What % of flagged theft/loss cases are logged, investigated, and closed with a documented outcome?
• Does Closed-Circuit Television (CCTV) and access-control cover all high-risk zones (dock, storage, packing)?
• Is CCTV footage reviewed proactively, or only after an incident occurs?
• Is the theft/loss rate tracked monthly, and is there a declining trend?

score_1_desc:
No defined process architecture for the end-to-end material and information flow.
Under 30% of individual processes have a documented flow diagram or defined steps.
score_2_desc:
A process architecture is sketched informally, not documented or shared.
30-50% of individual processes have a documented flow diagram/steps.
score_3_desc:
A defined process architecture exists, covering the major material and information flows.
50-75% of individual processes have documented flow diagrams/steps, reviewed annually.
score_4_desc:
Process architecture is documented and version-controlled, covering the full material and information flow.
75-95% of individual processes have documented flow diagrams/steps, reviewed twice a year.
score_5_desc:
Process architecture is fully documented, version-controlled, and used as the reference model for onboarding and audits.
Over 95% of individual processes have documented flow diagrams/steps, reviewed quarterly with zero undocumented recurring processes.
indicative_scoring_questions:
• Is there a documented process architecture covering the end-to-end material and information flow, and is it version-controlled?
• What % of individual processes have a documented flow diagram or defined steps?
• How often is the process architecture/flow documentation reviewed?
• Is the process architecture used as a reference model for onboarding and audits?

score_1_desc:
No defined ownership matrix for process steps.
Under 30% of processes have a named owner.
score_2_desc: Ownership is assigned informally, undocumented, for 30-50% of processes.
score_3_desc: A Responsible/Accountable/Consulted/Informed (RACI)-style ownership matrix is documented for 50-75% of processes, reviewed annually.
score_4_desc: A RACI-style ownership matrix is documented and version-controlled for 75-95% of processes, reviewed twice a year with defined escalation owners.
score_5_desc: A RACI-style ownership matrix covers over 95% of processes, version-controlled, reviewed quarterly, with zero processes lacking a named owner.
indicative_scoring_questions:
• What % of process steps have a named, documented owner?
• Is there a Responsible/Accountable/Consulted/Informed (RACI)-style ownership matrix, and is it version-controlled?
• How often is the ownership matrix reviewed?
• Are escalation owners defined within the matrix?

score_1_desc:
Under 30% of standard and exception scenarios are documented in Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs).
No approval matrix exists for exception/deviation handling.
score_2_desc:
30-50% of scenarios documented.
Exception flows are largely undocumented.
Exception approvals are handled ad hoc, without a defined approval level.
score_3_desc:
50-75% of scenarios documented, including major exception scenarios.
An approval matrix (who can approve what exception, at what level) is defined but covers under 50% of exception scenarios.
score_4_desc:
75-95% of scenarios documented and version-controlled, reviewed twice a year.
The exception approval matrix covers 50-90% of exception scenarios with a documented approval path.
score_5_desc:
Over 95% of standard and exception scenarios are documented, digitized, and reviewed quarterly, with zero undocumented recurring exceptions.
The exception approval matrix covers over 90% of exception scenarios, each with a documented, enforced approval path.
indicative_scoring_questions:
• What % of standard and exception scenarios are documented in Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs)?
• Is there a defined approval matrix specifying who can approve which exception, at what level?
• What % of exception scenarios have a documented, enforced approval path?
• How often is the exception/approval documentation reviewed, and is it digitized?

score_1_desc:
No defined mandatory scan points across the material journey.
Where scans exist, they are skippable, and traceability cannot be reconstructed end-to-end.
score_2_desc:
Mandatory scan points are defined for under 30% of the required journey stages.
Scans can be bypassed, leaving traceability gaps.
score_3_desc:
Mandatory scan points are defined for 30-60% of the required journey stages, covering the major handover points.
Scans are enforced (non-skippable) for under 60% of defined points.
score_4_desc:
Mandatory scan points are defined for 60-90% of the required journey stages, rationalized to the fewest points that still preserve full traceability.
Scans are enforced (non-skippable) for 60-95% of defined points.
score_5_desc:
Mandatory scan points cover over 90% of required journey stages, rationalized to the minimum set that still delivers complete end-to-end traceability.
Every defined scan point is enforced (non-skippable), with zero traceability gaps.
indicative_scoring_questions:
• Are mandatory scan points defined across the material journey, and what % of required journey stages do they cover?
• What % of defined scan points are enforced as non-skippable?
• Can end-to-end traceability be reconstructed from scan data, or are there gaps?
• Are scan points rationalized to the minimum set that still preserves full traceability?

score_1_desc:
0-1 of the 5 demand-planning layers (baseline/historical, seasonal & festive, event-based/sales, time-of-day, area/hyperlocal behavior) in use.
Forecast accuracy under 60%.
Hourly-volatility and Stock-Keeping Unit (SKU)-level inaccuracy are not analyzed, and new-store locations run on no meaningful demand data (pure guesswork).
score_2_desc:
2 layers active.
Forecast accuracy 60-75%.
Hourly volatility and hyperlocal (area-level) variation are acknowledged but not modeled.
New stores use a flat citywide/category average with no ramp-up curve.
score_3_desc:
3 layers active (e.g., baseline + seasonal/festive + event-based).
Forecast accuracy 75-85%.
Time-of-day demand curves are tracked for under 50% of SKUs/stores.
Hyperlocal (area-behavior) variation is factored in for high-volume stores only.
New stores follow a defined but generic ramp-up curve.
score_4_desc:
4 of the 5 layers active (typically missing time-of-day or area-behavior).
Forecast accuracy 85-95%.
Time-of-day and hyperlocal demand patterns are modeled for 70-90% of stores.
SKU-level forecast error is tracked and root-caused monthly.
New-store data gaps are bridged with a comparable-store proxy model for the first 4-6 weeks.
score_5_desc:
All 5 layers active and continuously calibrated against actuals (baseline, seasonal/festive, event-based, time-of-day, hyperlocal/area-behavior).
Forecast accuracy above 95%, directly driving the fill-rate Key Performance Indicator (KPI).
Hourly volatility and SKU-level accuracy are tracked in real time with automated recalibration.
New-store demand gaps are closed within 2-4 weeks via a proxy-to-actual transition model.
indicative_scoring_questions:
• How many of the 5 demand-planning layers (baseline/historical, seasonal & festive, event-based/sales, time-of-day, area/hyperlocal behavior) are actively used?
• What is the current forecast accuracy %, and does it directly drive the fill-rate Key Performance Indicator (KPI)?
• Is hourly-volatility and Stock-Keeping Unit (SKU)-level forecast error tracked and root-caused?
• How are new-store demand gaps bridged - flat citywide average, generic ramp-up curve, or a comparable-store proxy model?

score_1_desc:
0-1 of the 5 inventory-planning components (regular+buffer stock, seasonal buffer of +15-20%, festive buffer of +50-100%, First-Expired-First-Out (FEFO) discipline for fresh/perishable SKUs, Stock-Keeping Unit (SKU) assortment) defined.
Stockout/excess (waste) incidents affect over 20% of SKUs monthly.
Batch/expiry tracking is manual or absent, and shelf-life-driven markdowns/write-offs are not visible until after the fact.
score_2_desc:
2 components defined.
Incidents affect 10-20% of SKUs monthly.
FEFO is followed inconsistently, with batch mismanagement (wrong batch picked/dispatched) as a regular occurrence.
Inventory visibility lags actual stock by more than a day.
score_3_desc:
3 components defined (e.g., regular+buffer stock, one of seasonal/festive buffer, and a defined SKU assortment).
Incidents affect 5-10% of SKUs monthly.
FEFO is enforced for the majority of fresh SKUs.
Batch-level visibility exists but is not real-time, creating an occasional stockout-vs-waste trade-off at the shelf-life boundary.
score_4_desc:
4 of the 5 components defined and reviewed monthly (seasonal +15-20% and festive +50-100% buffers both applied, FEFO enforced for fresh).
Incidents affect under 5% of SKUs monthly.
Batch/expiry data is visible near-real-time, keeping the stockout-vs-waste trade-off and batch mismanagement to isolated exceptions.
score_5_desc:
All 5 components defined, automated, and reviewed weekly (regular+buffer stock, seasonal +15-20% buffer, festive +50-100% buffer, FEFO for fresh, SKU assortment).
Incidents affect under 2% of SKUs monthly.
Batch/expiry visibility is real-time and system-enforced, eliminating batch mismanagement and holding the stockout-vs-waste trade-off within a defined tolerance.
indicative_scoring_questions:
• How many of the 5 inventory-planning components (regular + buffer stock, seasonal buffer of +15-20%, festive buffer of +50-100%, First-Expired-First-Out (FEFO) discipline, Stock-Keeping Unit (SKU) assortment) are defined?
• What % of SKUs are affected by stockout or excess/waste incidents monthly?
• Is FEFO enforced for fresh SKUs, and how often does batch mismanagement (wrong batch picked/dispatched) occur?
• Is batch/expiry data visible in real time, or does it lag actual stock?

score_1_desc:
Replenishment triggered manually, irregularly.
No formula (Forecast Demand + Safety Stock - Current Inventory) used.
No wave structure, no min-max/reorder-point model.
No emergency top-up process for stockout risk.
Days of Inventory (DoI) not tracked.
Partial fulfillment, dock congestion, storage overflow common and unmanaged.
score_2_desc:
Formula-based replenishment defined, run less than once a day.
Wave split ad hoc.
Min-max/reorder-point trigger defined for under 30% of SKUs.
Emergency top-up handled ad hoc, no SLA.
DoI tracked in aggregate only.
Partial fulfillment and storage overflow incidents frequent.
score_3_desc:
Replenishment run once a day, on the standard formula.
Wave timing fixed, not demand-driven.
Min-max/reorder-point triggers cover 30-60% of SKUs.
Emergency top-up process exists, manually invoked.
DoI tracked by category.
Dock congestion from receipts reviewed, not systematically avoided.
score_4_desc:
Replenishment run twice a day on a fixed clock.
Wave split defined (e.g., 70% night / 30% morning), moving toward demand-driven.
Not yet tied live to real dark-store demand signals.
Min-max/reorder-point triggers cover 60-90% of SKUs.
SLA-bound emergency top-up process in place.
DoI tracked by Stock-Keeping Unit (SKU) against a target band.
Dock congestion, storage overflow from receipts reduced to isolated exceptions.
score_5_desc:
Automatic Replenishment System (ARS) runs the cycle twice a day.
Driven by real dark-store demand signals, not a fixed schedule.
Approximately 70% of replenishment executed at night, 30% morning/afternoon.
Lead-time-adjusted safety stock; under 2% stockout rate at dark stores.
Min-max/reorder-point triggers cover over 90% of SKUs.
Fully integrated with the automated, SLA-bound emergency top-up process.
DoI tracked by SKU in real time against target bands.
Dock congestion, storage overflow from receipts eliminated via slotted receiving.
Partial-fulfillment incidents root-caused monthly.
indicative_scoring_questions:
• Is replenishment formula-based (Forecast Demand + Safety Stock - Current Inventory), and how many times a day does it run?
• Is the wave split (e.g., ~70% night / 30% day) defined, and is it driven by real dark-store demand signals or a fixed schedule?
• What % of Stock-Keeping Units (SKUs) have a min-max/reorder-point trigger defined?
• Is there a Service Level Agreement (SLA)-bound emergency top-up process for stockout risk?
• Is Days of Inventory (DoI) tracked by SKU against a target band?
• How frequent are dock congestion, storage overflow, or partial-fulfillment incidents?

score_1_desc:
0-2 of 6 roles (inbound, outbound/picking, packing, put-away, supervisory, security) have defined manpower planning.
Staffing variance exceeds 20%.
No surge-planning mechanism for demand spikes and no defined gig-workforce flexibility strategy.
Staffing decisions ignore diurnal (hour-of-day) demand variability, and attrition/gig-supply risk are not tracked.
score_2_desc:
3 roles planned.
Staffing variance 15-20%.
Surge planning is reactive (arranged only after a spike is already underway).
Gig-workforce usage is ad hoc with no defined flex ratio.
Diurnal variability is acknowledged but not built into shift design.
Attrition is tracked but not analyzed.
score_3_desc:
4 roles planned.
Variance 10-15%.
A surge-planning trigger and a defined gig-to-permanent flex ratio exist for under 60% of shifts.
Shift design accounts for diurnal variability for the main peak window only.
Attrition and gig-supply risk are tracked monthly without a mitigation plan.
score_4_desc:
5 roles planned with shift-level granularity.
Variance 5-10%.
Surge planning and a defined gig-flex ratio are applied on 60-90% of shifts, with shift design built around the full diurnal demand curve.
Attrition and gig-supply risk are tracked with an active mitigation/backup-pool plan.
score_5_desc:
All 6 roles planned with daily granularity and capacity buffers.
Variance under 5%.
Surge planning and gig-flex ratio are applied on over 90% of shifts with capacity buffers pre-built into the roster.
Shift design is fully diurnal-curve-driven.
Attrition is held below a defined benchmark and gig-supply risk is mitigated via a pre-qualified backup pool, reviewed monthly.
indicative_scoring_questions:
• How many of the 6 roles (inbound, outbound/picking, packing, put-away, supervisory, security) have defined manpower planning?
• What is the current staffing variance %?
• Is there a surge-planning mechanism for demand spikes, and a defined gig-to-permanent flex ratio?
• Does shift design account for diurnal (hour-of-day) demand variability?
• Is attrition and gig-supply risk tracked, with an active mitigation/backup-pool plan?

score_1_desc:
Fewer than 1 planned warehouse-to-dark-store replenishment cycle per day.
Dispatch is ad hoc.
No route or truck-load optimization applied (vehicles dispatched part-full, unoptimized routes).
Freezer/cold-chain capacity not factored into network planning.
Inbound to not-yet-live (pre-live) dark stores unplanned, causes downstream issues.
score_2_desc:
1 replenishment cycle per day.
Wave split not defined.
Route/truck-load optimization applied to under 30% of dispatch routes.
Freezer-capacity constraints identified only after a breach.
Pre-live-store inward handled same as live-store inward, no distinction.
score_3_desc:
1-2 cycles per day with a defined split (approximately 70/30), adherence under 70%.
Route/truck-load optimization covers 30-60% of dispatch routes.
Freezer/cold-chain capacity checked before dispatch, for temperature-sensitive SKUs only.
Pre-live dark-store inward follows a separate but informal process.
score_4_desc:
2 cycles per day with a 70/30 (or optimized) split, adherence 70-90%.
Route/truck-load optimization covers 60-90% of dispatch routes, holding Orders Per Hour (OPH) close to target.
Freezer/cold-chain capacity planned ahead of dispatch, across all temperature zones.
Pre-live dark-store inward follows a defined, separate Standard Operating Procedure (SOP).
score_5_desc:
2 or more cycles per day, wave-split adherence above 90%, dynamically adjusted to dark-store stock positions in real time.
Route/truck-load optimization covers over 90% of dispatch routes, OPH consistently at or above target.
Freezer/cold-chain capacity dynamically planned, zero temperature-zone breaches.
Pre-live dark-store inward fully governed by a dedicated SOP, zero cross-over incidents into live operations.
indicative_scoring_questions:
• How many planned warehouse-to-dark-store replenishment cycles run per day, and what is the wave-split (e.g., ~70/30) adherence %?
• What % of dispatch routes have route/truck-load optimization applied, and how does Orders Per Hour (OPH) compare to target?
• Is freezer/cold-chain capacity planned ahead of dispatch across all temperature zones, or discovered only after a breach?
• Is inbound to pre-live (not-yet-live) dark stores governed by a separate, defined Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)?

score_1_desc:
Fill rate under 70%.
No defined D-minus planning day; replenishment planning done same-day or reactively.
No visibility into the planning-to-dispatch window at all.
score_2_desc:
Fill rate 70-80%.
Planning runs on D-1 (plan and dispatch the same day), used inconsistently.
D-1 planning compresses the processing window, creating a bottleneck between material arrival and dispatch.
score_3_desc:
Fill rate 80-90%.
D-1 planning day formally defined and followed for FnV/dry categories.
The D-1 processing-window bottleneck is recognized but not yet resolved by moving to D-2.
score_4_desc:
Fill rate 90-95%.
Planning cycle is moving from D-1 to D-2 for the majority of categories/stores; variance root-caused monthly.
Where D-2 is adopted, material arrives D-1 and is processed/dispatched the same day (D-1), sale at dark store on D.
score_5_desc:
Fill rate above 95% (benchmark).
D-2 planning followed on 100% of days: plan on D-2, material arrives at the warehouse D-1, processed and dispatched D-1 (same day as arrival), sale at dark store on D.
Over/under-planning variance under 5%.
indicative_scoring_questions:
• What is the current fill rate %?
• Is replenishment planned on a defined D-1 or D-2 cycle, and is it followed consistently across categories/stores?
• Is there a bottleneck between material arrival and dispatch caused by a compressed, same-day planning window?
• What is the over/under-planning variance %, and is it root-caused monthly?

score_1_desc:
Supplier performance not tracked in any structured way.
No vendor fill rate, QC reject rate, or vendor-attributable RTV rate.
On-Time-In-Full (OTIF) neither defined nor measured.
Lead time undefined, even at vendor level, let alone per SKU.
Sourcing decisions made with zero supplier-risk visibility.
score_2_desc:
One metric (typically OTIF) tracked in aggregate, no vendor breakdown.
Vendor fill rate, QC reject rate, RTV rate known anecdotally only.
Lead time defined per vendor for under 30% of vendors.
Lead time never defined per Stock-Keeping Unit (SKU).
score_3_desc:
OTIF and vendor fill rate tracked by vendor, reviewed quarterly.
QC reject rate and vendor-attributable Return to Vendor (RTV) rate tracked for some vendors/SKUs.
Not yet linked to sourcing/allocation decisions.
Lead time defined per vendor for the majority of vendors.
Per-SKU lead time defined for under 30% of SKUs.
score_4_desc:
OTIF, vendor fill rate, QC reject rate, RTV rate tracked by vendor.
Reviewed monthly, feeding a supplier scorecard.
Lead time defined per vendor per SKU for 60-90% of combinations.
Sourcing allocation adjusted for chronic OTIF/quality/RTV underperformers.
score_5_desc:
OTIF, vendor fill rate, QC reject rate, RTV rate tracked by vendor and SKU in real time.
Automated scorecard drives sourcing/allocation and vendor tiering.
Lead time defined per vendor per SKU for over 90% of combinations, kept current.
OTIF held above a defined benchmark (e.g., 95%+).
Quarterly vendor business reviews close the loop on quality, fill rate, RTV.
indicative_scoring_questions:
• Is On-Time-In-Full (OTIF) tracked by vendor, and what is the current OTIF %?
• Are vendor fill rate, Quality Check (QC) reject rate, and vendor-attributable Return to Vendor (RTV) rate tracked by vendor and Stock-Keeping Unit (SKU)?
• What % of vendor-SKU combinations have a defined, current lead time?
• Is sourcing/allocation adjusted based on a supplier scorecard, with quarterly vendor business reviews?

score_1_desc: Indent is not reconciled against actual inward/dispatch at all, or the variance exceeds 30% where checked.
score_2_desc: Indent-vs-actual variance runs at 20-30%, reconciled only in aggregate.
score_3_desc: Indent-vs-actual variance runs at 10-20%, reconciled daily for the majority of SKUs/stores.
score_4_desc: Indent-vs-actual variance runs at 5-10%, reconciled daily with root cause reviewed monthly.
score_5_desc: Indent-vs-actual variance is held under 5%, reconciled in real time and reported as a standing indent-accuracy Key Performance Indicator (KPI) alongside forecast accuracy.
indicative_scoring_questions:
• Is indent reconciled against actual inward/dispatch quantity, and what is the current variance %?
• How frequently is this reconciliation done - in aggregate, daily, or real-time?
• Is the variance root-caused, and how often?
• Is indent accuracy tracked as a standing Key Performance Indicator (KPI) alongside forecast accuracy?

score_1_desc: First-In-First-Out (FIFO) compliance for inventory rotation (distinct from the dock-sequencing FIFO in A1.4) runs under 50%, with picking/putaway routinely bypassing the oldest-stock-first rule.
score_2_desc: FIFO compliance runs at 50-70%, followed inconsistently across zones.
score_3_desc: FIFO compliance runs at 70-85%, enforced for the majority of zones but not system-validated.
score_4_desc: FIFO compliance runs at 85-95%, system-guided for putaway and picking across most zones.
score_5_desc: FIFO compliance exceeds 95%, system-enforced at putaway and picking with exceptions flagged automatically.
indicative_scoring_questions:
• What is the current First-In-First-Out (FIFO) compliance % for inventory rotation (picking/putaway following oldest-stock-first)?
• Is FIFO enforced consistently across all zones, or followed inconsistently?
• Is FIFO compliance system-guided/system-validated at putaway and picking, or manually tracked?
• Are FIFO exceptions flagged automatically?

score_1_desc:
Inventory accuracy (system vs. physical stock) runs under 90%.
No regular cycle-count process or defined frequency.
No cycle-count reports published.
SKU coverage over any cycle period unknown; likely permanently-uncounted SKUs.
score_2_desc:
Inventory accuracy runs at 90-95%.
Cycle counts happen ad hoc, no defined frequency per location/SKU.
Reports, where produced, are informal, not regularly published.
SKU coverage over a cycle period not tracked.
score_3_desc:
Inventory accuracy runs at 95-98%.
A defined cycle-count frequency exists per location/SKU, followed for most locations.
Cycle-count reports published periodically.
Full SKU coverage over the cycle period targeted, not verified.
score_4_desc:
Inventory accuracy runs at 98-99.5%.
Cycle counts run weekly against the defined frequency; variance root-caused.
Cycle-count reports published weekly.
Coverage mechanism confirms most SKUs counted within the cycle period; isolated gaps remain.
score_5_desc:
Inventory accuracy exceeds 99.5%, via continuous/perpetual cycle counting with real-time variance alerts.
Cycle-count frequency defined and adhered to for 100% of locations/SKUs.
Cycle-count reports published in real time/daily.
Full SKU coverage over the cycle period verified; zero permanently-uncounted SKUs.
indicative_scoring_questions:
• What is the current inventory accuracy % (system vs. physical stock)?
• Is there a defined cycle-count frequency per location/Stock-Keeping Unit (SKU), and is it followed?
• How often are cycle-count reports published - ad hoc, periodic, weekly, or real-time?
• Is full SKU coverage over the cycle period verified, or are there likely permanently-uncounted SKUs?

score_1_desc: Expiry loss exceeds 3% of inventory value/sales, not reconciled against First-Expired-First-Out (FEFO) compliance.
score_2_desc: Expiry loss runs at 2-3%.
score_3_desc: Expiry loss runs at 1-2%, tracked monthly but not yet linked to FEFO compliance.
score_4_desc: Expiry loss runs at 0.5-1%, reviewed monthly against FEFO compliance to close the loop.
score_5_desc: Expiry loss is held under 0.5%, tracked in real time and directly reconciled against FEFO/First-In-First-Out (FIFO) compliance.
indicative_scoring_questions:
• What is the current expiry loss % (value of expired inventory / total sales value)?
• Is expiry loss tracked monthly or in real time?
• Is expiry loss reconciled against First-Expired-First-Out (FEFO)/First-In-First-Out (FIFO) compliance to close the loop?

score_1_desc: Absenteeism exceeds 10%, not linked to staffing-variance root cause.
score_2_desc: Absenteeism runs at 7-10%, tracked but not analyzed.
score_3_desc: Absenteeism runs at 5-7%, tracked daily and reviewed as one driver of staffing variance.
score_4_desc: Absenteeism runs at 3-5%, tracked daily with a defined threshold and reviewed alongside attrition.
score_5_desc: Absenteeism is held under 3%, tracked daily and reviewed jointly with attrition and gig-supply risk as the standing staffing-variance root-cause set.
indicative_scoring_questions:
• What is the current absenteeism % (manpower absent / manpower rostered)?
• Is absenteeism tracked daily, with a defined threshold?
• Is absenteeism reviewed as a driver of staffing variance, alongside attrition and gig-supply risk?

subpoint_name: Inward Accuracy (Actual Arrived Qty vs. Indent)
score_1_desc: Inward quantity deviates from Indent by more than 25%, with no reconciled tracking.
score_2_desc: Inward deviates from Indent by 15-25%, tracked in aggregate only.
score_3_desc: Inward deviates from Indent by 10-15%, reconciled daily for FnV/dry categories.
score_4_desc: Inward deviates from Indent by 5-10%, reconciled daily with variance root-caused monthly.
score_5_desc: Inward deviates from Indent by under 5%, reconciled in real time as part of the daily planning-cycle Key Performance Indicator (KPI) set.
indicative_scoring_questions:
• What is the current deviation % between actual inward quantity and indent?
• Is this reconciled daily, and for which categories (e.g., Fruits & Vegetables (FnV)/dry)?
• Is the variance root-caused, and how often?
• Is inward accuracy tracked in real time as part of the daily planning-cycle Key Performance Indicator (KPI) set?

subpoint_name: Dispatched Accuracy (Actual Dispatched Qty vs. Plan)
score_1_desc: Dispatched quantity deviates from the plan by more than 25%, with no reconciled tracking.
score_2_desc: Dispatched deviates from plan by 15-25%, tracked in aggregate only.
score_3_desc: Dispatched deviates from plan by 10-15%, reconciled daily for FnV/dry categories.
score_4_desc: Dispatched deviates from plan by 5-10%, reconciled daily with variance root-caused monthly.
score_5_desc: Dispatched deviates from plan by under 5%, reconciled in real time alongside fill rate as part of the daily planning-cycle Key Performance Indicator (KPI) set.
indicative_scoring_questions:
• What is the current deviation % between actual dispatched quantity and the plan?
• Is this reconciled daily, and for which categories?
• Is the variance root-caused monthly?
• Is dispatch accuracy tracked alongside fill rate as part of the daily planning-cycle Key Performance Indicator (KPI) set?

score_1_desc:
Facility throughput under 60% of the Fruits & Vegetables (FnV) benchmark (below 2.4 units/sq ft).
Dispatch capacity not benchmarked against warehouse area at all.
score_2_desc:
Throughput at 60-75% of the FnV benchmark.
Dispatch capacity vs. warehouse area is not yet validated.
score_3_desc:
Throughput at 75-90% of the FnV benchmark (approximately 3-3.6 units/sq ft).
Dispatch capacity is estimated against warehouse area but not formally validated.
score_4_desc:
Throughput at 90-100% of the FnV benchmark (4 units/sq ft).
Outbound dispatch capacity validated at approximately 4x warehouse area.
score_5_desc:
Throughput consistently at or above the FnV benchmark (4+ units/sq ft).
Dispatch capacity engineered and validated at exactly 4x warehouse area (e.g., a 50,000 sq ft facility supporting 200,000-unit dispatch capacity), reviewed quarterly.
indicative_scoring_questions:
• What is current throughput (units dispatched per sq ft per day), and how does it compare to the Fruits & Vegetables (FnV) benchmark of 2.4-4+ units/sq ft?
• Has dispatch capacity been validated against warehouse area (target ~4x)? Ask to see the calculation.
• Is this validation reviewed on a set cadence (e.g., quarterly), or was it a one-time exercise?
• Is throughput trending up, flat, or down over recent periods?

score_1_desc:
Layout not benchmarked against Selective Pallet Racking (SPR)/Multi-Tier Shelving (MTS) design standards.
Storage-area ratio undefined or deviates over 70% from the 50-60% norm.
score_2_desc:
Partial benchmarking against SPR/MTS design standards.
Storage ratio in the 60-70% band (too high, indicating processing-area shortfall) or below 40%.
score_3_desc:
Storage area at 50-60% of total footprint, per design norm.
Aisle widths (~10 ft) and beam lengths (~2.4m) mostly conform to standard.
score_4_desc:
Full conformance to SPR/MTS specifications (aisle width, 100mm overhang, 3-4 ft sprinkler clearance).
Storage ratio at 50-55%, or up to 60% for high-inventory/smaller-city sites.
Density near 22.5 units/sq ft.
score_5_desc:
Layout fully optimized, including narrow-aisle configurations where applicable.
Density at 22.5 units/sq ft with 100% spec conformance.
Storage ratio precisely tuned to inventory-days requirement.
indicative_scoring_questions:
• Has the layout been benchmarked against Selective Pallet Racking (SPR)/Multi-Tier Shelving (MTS) design standards? Ask for evidence.
• What % of total footprint is storage area (design norm: 50-60%)?
• Do aisle widths (~10 ft) and beam lengths (~2.4m) conform to standard? Check on the floor.
• What is current storage density (units/sq ft) versus the ~22.5 units/sq ft target?
• Is the storage ratio tuned to inventory-days requirement, or fixed regardless of demand?
• Are narrow-aisle configurations used where applicable?

score_1_desc:
0-2 of the core cost components tracked (manpower, material supply, packaging, electricity, depreciation, rent).
Other relevant components (e.g., security, maintenance) not considered.
No per-facility tracking; no periodic review.
Cost per Order not understood as derived - untracked, or duplicated as a separate exercise.
score_2_desc:
3 of the core components tracked, blended across facilities, not per facility.
Additional components (security, maintenance, etc.) not yet considered.
Reviewed annually.
Cost per Order, where mentioned, not linked back to Cost per Unit.
score_3_desc:
4-5 of the core components tracked per facility.
At least one other relevant component (e.g., security, maintenance) included where material.
Reviewed quarterly.
Cost per Order understood as Cost per Unit x Units per Order, but still separately tracked in places.
score_4_desc:
All 6 core components, plus other relevant components, tracked consistently per facility.
Reviewed monthly, feeding cost-per-unit optimization actions.
Cost per Order consistently derived as Cost per Unit x Units per Order, not double-tracked.
score_5_desc:
Full cost-component coverage (core plus all other relevant components) tracked across every facility.
Reviewed monthly or more often, with a documented downward cost-per-unit trend.
Cost per Order always derived (Cost per Unit x Units per Order), never separately tracked.
Reviewed alongside Cost per Unit as one unified view.
indicative_scoring_questions:
• How many of the 6 core cost components (manpower, material supply, packaging, electricity, depreciation, rent) are tracked?
• Are costs tracked per facility, or only blended across facilities?
• Are other relevant components (e.g., security, maintenance) included where material?
• How frequently is cost per unit reviewed - annually, quarterly, or monthly?
• Is Cost per Order derived as Cost per Unit x Units per Order, or tracked separately (double-counted)?
• Is there a documented downward cost-per-unit trend?

subpoint_name: Project Planning & Governance (Charter, Timeline, Cost Control)
score_1_desc:
No formal project charter, scope definition, or Gantt chart is used for planning/execution.
Timelines and budgets are not documented.
Delivery is tracked informally, with over 50% of projects (of any type - warehouse design/expansion, systems rollout, process change, etc.) running behind schedule or over budget with no visibility into the cause.
score_2_desc:
A basic project charter (scope/objective) is drafted for under 40% of projects.
No Gantt chart or formal milestone timeline is maintained.
Schedule or cost overrun exceeds 30% on the majority of tracked projects.
score_3_desc:
A project charter (scope, objective, stakeholders, budget) and a Gantt chart with defined milestones are used for 40-70% of projects.
Milestone/timeline adherence is reviewed periodically (e.g., monthly), but cost tracking against budget is inconsistent.
Schedule or cost overrun is in the 15-30% band.
score_4_desc:
A project charter and Gantt chart with milestone-level timelines are mandatory and used for 70-95% of projects.
Progress and cost are reviewed on a defined cadence (e.g., weekly) against the charter baseline.
Schedule/cost overrun held under 15%, with variances root-caused.
score_5_desc:
Over 95% of projects (irrespective of type) are governed by a formal charter and Gantt chart with baselined milestones, tracked in real time against a defined ownership/Responsible, Accountable, Consulted, Informed (RACI) matrix.
Over 90% of projects are delivered on time and within the approved budget (schedule/cost overrun under 5%), with lessons-learned closed out post-project.
indicative_scoring_questions:
• Is a formal project charter (scope, objective, stakeholders, budget) used, and for what % of projects?
• Is a Gantt chart with defined milestones maintained?
• What % of projects run over schedule or over budget, and by how much?
• How often is progress/cost reviewed against the charter baseline - monthly, weekly, or real-time?
• Is there a defined Responsible, Accountable, Consulted, Informed (RACI) matrix for project ownership?
• Are lessons-learned closed out post-project?

score_1_desc: Utility cost per sqft runs more than 20% over the approved budget/benchmark, with no per-sqft normalization tracked.
score_2_desc: Utility cost per sqft runs 10-20% over budget/benchmark.
score_3_desc: Utility cost per sqft runs within 10% of budget/benchmark, tracked quarterly.
score_4_desc: Utility cost per sqft runs at or below budget/benchmark, tracked monthly.
score_5_desc: Utility cost per sqft runs consistently below budget/benchmark with a documented downward trend, tracked monthly or more frequently.
indicative_scoring_questions:
• What is utility cost per sq ft versus the approved budget/benchmark?
• Is utility cost normalized per sq ft, or only tracked in aggregate?
• How often is it reviewed - quarterly, monthly, or more frequently?
• Is there a documented downward trend in utility cost per sq ft?

score_1_desc:
0% of inbound Fruits & Vegetables (FnV) volume routed through a Collection Center (CC).
No financial justification test exists.
CC cost + middle-mile leg cost vs. Sorting & Grading (S&G)/packing savings - question never asked.
score_2_desc:
Under 20% of volume routed via a CC.
Where a CC exists, its financial justification is not calculated.
CC cost + CC-to-warehouse middle-mile leg vs. reduced S&G/packing load and net landing cost - untested.
score_3_desc:
20-50% of volume via a CC, reducing first-mile disruption.
A financial justification test is calculated.
Result is unverified, or shows the CC is not clearly paying for itself.
score_4_desc:
50-80% of volume via a CC, with a defined sorting/grading/packing split.
Financial justification test calculated for the majority of CCs.
CC-plus-middle-mile cost shown below warehouse S&G/packing savings and net landing-cost reduction.
score_5_desc:
Over 80% of volume via a CC.
Every CC passes the financial justification test.
CC-plus-middle-mile cost verified below the combined S&G/packing savings and net landing-cost reduction it generates.
Fully optimized first-mile network, measurably reducing cost-per-unit quarter-on-quarter.
indicative_scoring_questions:
• What % of inbound Fruits & Vegetables (FnV) volume is routed through a Collection Center (CC)?
• Has a financial justification test been calculated for the CC (CC cost plus middle-mile leg versus Sorting & Grading (S&G)/packing savings)?
• Does the CC pass this test - is CC-plus-middle-mile cost below the S&G/packing savings and net landing-cost reduction it generates?
• Is this reviewed periodically, and is there a quarter-on-quarter cost-per-unit reduction trend?

score_1_desc:
Under 50% of CC dispatches meet the 3:00 PM cutoff.
Frequent arrivals past 9:00 PM.
Cutoff set arbitrarily, no link to warehouse's remaining packing/labeling/allocation workload or its dispatch wave.
score_2_desc:
50-70% adherence to the 3:00 PM dispatch / 9:00 PM arrival cutoffs.
Cutoff timing not designed around the warehouse's processing buffer.
A late CC dispatch regularly squeezes the warehouse's own pre-dispatch work.
score_3_desc:
70-85% adherence. Material typically arrives by 8-9 PM, packing done by 11:30 PM.
Cutoff-to-buffer link is recognized but not formally designed in.
score_4_desc:
85-95% adherence. Arrival consistently by 7-8 PM, processing complete by 12:00 AM, FnV dispatch by 1:00 PM.
CC cutoff (for a CC 50-70 km from the warehouse, typically 2:30-3:00 PM) explicitly leaves a defined buffer for warehouse packing/labeling/allocation ahead of its dispatch wave.
score_5_desc:
Over 95% adherence to the full cutoff chain (2:30-3:00 PM CC dispatch, 7-8 PM arrival, 12 AM processing complete, 1 PM FnV dispatch), tracked daily on an SLA dashboard.
Cutoff is explicitly buffer-designed against warehouse processing capacity.
Zero downstream squeeze incidents at the warehouse's outbound wave.
indicative_scoring_questions:
• What % of CC dispatches meet the defined cutoff (e.g., 2:30-3:00 PM) and arrival window (e.g., 7-9 PM)?
• Is the cutoff explicitly designed around the warehouse's remaining packing/labeling/allocation workload, or set arbitrarily?
• Does a late CC dispatch regularly squeeze the warehouse's pre-dispatch work?
• Is adherence tracked daily on a Service Level Agreement (SLA) dashboard?
• Are there zero downstream squeeze incidents at the warehouse's outbound wave?

score_1_desc:
No defined processing split between Collection Center (CC) and warehouse.
Allocation decided ad hoc daily, not tied to supply-assurance or processing-capability.
Packing/stickering happens only at the warehouse, not tracked as a CC activity.
No weight verification at CC-to-warehouse handoff.
score_2_desc:
Split defined loosely, not documented as a fixed percentage.
Not linked to supply-assurance/processing-capability at either site.
Packing/stickering at the CC, where it happens, untracked and inconsistent.
Handoff weight checked manually if at all, no defined method.
score_3_desc:
Split formally defined as a fixed percentage (e.g., 70% CC / 30% warehouse), followed on over 70% of days.
Set as an arbitrary ratio, not matched to supply-assurance/processing-capability.
Packing/stickering at the CC tracked for the majority of eligible volume.
Handoff weight verification manual, done for most CC-to-warehouse dispatches.
score_4_desc:
Defined split followed on over 90% of days.
Reviewed monthly against volume, cost-per-unit impact, and supply-assurance/processing-capability at each site.
Packing/stickering at the CC standard practice, tracked for over 90% of eligible volume.
Internet of Things (IoT)-based weight verification used for the majority of handoffs.
score_5_desc:
Split optimized and reviewed quarterly, followed on over 95% of days.
Documented rationale explicitly matches the ratio to supply-assurance and processing-capability.
Packing/stickering at the CC fully systemized, covering effectively all eligible volume.
IoT-based weight verification covers 100% of handoffs, zero unverified transfers.
indicative_scoring_questions:
• Is there a defined CC-vs-warehouse processing split (e.g., 70/30), documented as a fixed percentage?
• Is the split tied to supply-assurance/processing-capability at each site, or set arbitrarily?
• What % of days is the defined split actually followed?
• Is packing/stickering done and tracked as a CC activity?
• Is weight verified at the CC-to-warehouse handoff - manually, or via Internet of Things (IoT)-based sensors?
• What % of handoffs have IoT-based weight-verification coverage?

score_1_desc:
Unloading productivity not benchmarked by load type (packed vs bulk).
No target set.
score_2_desc:
Productivity tracked in aggregate only, below benchmark (under 400 units/person/hour packed.
Under 4 pallets/person/hour bulk).
score_3_desc: Productivity at benchmark for one load type only: 500 units/person/hour for packed material, or 5 pallets (125 crates)/person/hour for bulk - not both.
score_4_desc:
Productivity at benchmark for both load types (500 units/person/hour packed.
5 pallets or 125 crates/person/hour bulk), tracked daily.
score_5_desc: Productivity consistently at or above benchmark for both load types, tracked in real time, with variance-driven staffing adjustments.
indicative_scoring_questions:
• Is unloading productivity benchmarked separately by load type - packed versus bulk?
• What is current productivity (units/person/hour packed; pallets or crates/person/hour bulk) versus benchmark (500 units/person/hour packed; 5 pallets or 125 crates/person/hour bulk)?
• Is productivity tracked daily or in real time, or only periodically/in aggregate?
• Are staffing levels adjusted based on productivity variance?

score_1_desc:
Receiving not verified against inbound manifest.
Stock put away wherever space allows.
No defined putaway sequence.
Receipt-to-Goods Receipt Note (GRN) Turnaround Time (TAT) not measured.
GRN-to-Putaway TAT not measured.
No defined receiving model - tote-level scan-in vs. unit-wise GRN not distinguished.
Receiving accuracy not tracked, or under 90% where spot-checked.

Receiving checked against manifest for majority of inbound trips.
Check is manual, no system confirmation.
Putaway follows an informal, memory-based location pattern.
Receipt-to-GRN TAT and GRN-to-Putaway TAT logged inconsistently, not split as separate segments.
A receiving model (tote-level or unit-wise) is used but inconsistently, not tracked by type.
Receiving accuracy runs 90-95%.
score_3_desc:
Receiving verified against digital manifest for over 70% of inbound trips before putaway begins.
Defined rack/shelf locations exist for majority of SKUs and are followed.
Receipt-to-GRN TAT and GRN-to-Putaway TAT tracked as separate segments, reviewed weekly.
Receiving model (tote-level scan-in or unit-wise GRN) is defined and applied consistently for majority of SKUs.
Receiving accuracy runs 95-98%.
score_4_desc:
Receiving scanned against digital manifest for over 90% of inbound trips.
Short-receipt/excess auto-flagged.
Putaway is system-directed for over 90% of SKUs.
Receipt-to-GRN TAT and GRN-to-Putaway TAT tracked daily against defined targets.
Where tote-level receiving is used, tote-content integrity is spot-checked to validate reliability.
Receiving model choice is deliberate by SKU/vendor, not default.
Receiving accuracy runs 98-99.5%.
score_5_desc:
Receiving scanned end-to-end, zero manual reconciliation.
Short-receipt/excess auto-escalated in real time.
Putaway is system-directed for 100% of SKUs with real-time location confirmation.
Receipt-to-GRN TAT and GRN-to-Putaway TAT held under defined benchmarks, tracked in real time.
Receiving model applied consistently per SKU/vendor category.
Tote-content integrity validated in real time where tote-level receiving is used.
Receiving accuracy exceeds 99.5%.
indicative_scoring_questions:
• Is inbound receiving verified against a digital manifest before putaway begins, and for what % of trips?
• Is putaway system-directed to defined locations, or ad hoc/memory-based?
• Are Receipt-to-Goods Receipt Note (GRN) Turnaround Time (TAT) and GRN-to-Putaway TAT tracked as separate segments?
• Is there a defined receiving model - tote-level scan-in versus unit-wise GRN - applied consistently by SKU/vendor?
• Are short-receipt/excess auto-flagged or escalated in real time?
• What is current receiving accuracy %?

score_1_desc:
No defined picking or packing productivity target at the dark store.
Productivity not measured.
Order-Receipt-to-Order-Acceptance time not tracked.
Pick rate per person not tracked.
Units per order not tracked.
Order-Handover-to-Delivery-Agent time not tracked.
Not-Received (NR) % - ordered items unfulfillable due to shortage, expiry, or wastage - not tracked.

Order-Receipt-to-Order-Acceptance time and Order-Handover-to-Delivery-Agent time not measured.
Pick rate estimated occasionally, well outside the 13-16 second/unit benchmark.
NR% and shelf-level material availability known anecdotally, not measured.
Picking accuracy runs 95-97%.
