Picker and packer productivity (units/person/hour) tracked daily against target for majority of shifts.
Order-Receipt-to-Order-Acceptance time and units-per-order tracked for majority of orders.
Pick rate tracked for majority of shifts, trending toward the 13-16 second/unit/person benchmark.
NR% tracked weekly.
Shelf-level material availability tracked weekly.
Picking accuracy runs 97-99%, reviewed weekly.
score_4_desc:
Productivity tracked in real time per picker/packer via the order management system.
Under-performance flagged same-shift.
Order-Receipt-to-Order-Acceptance time and Order-Handover-to-Delivery-Agent time tracked for over 90% of orders.
Pick rate at or within the 13-16 second/unit/person benchmark for majority of shifts.
NR% root-caused weekly.
Shelf-level material availability tracked daily with low-availability alerts.
Picking accuracy runs 99-99.5%, root-caused weekly.
score_5_desc:
Productivity tracked in real time, benchmarked across dark stores.
Feeds automated staffing/roster adjustment.
Order-Receipt-to-Order-Acceptance time, pick rate, units per order, and Order-Handover-to-Delivery-Agent time tracked in real time end-to-end.
Pick rate consistently within the 13-16 second/unit/person benchmark.
NR% held near-zero, root-caused daily.
Shelf-level material availability tracked in real time.
Picking accuracy exceeds 99.5%, root-caused daily per picker.
indicative_scoring_questions:
• Is a picking/packing productivity target defined and tracked (units/person/hour), and how often - real-time, daily, weekly, or not at all?
• What is the current pick rate versus the 13-16 second/unit/person benchmark?
• Are Order-Receipt-to-Order-Acceptance time and Order-Handover-to-Delivery-Agent time tracked?
• What is current picking accuracy %?
• Is Not-Received (NR) % - items unfulfillable due to shortage, expiry, or wastage - tracked and root-caused?
• Is shelf-level material availability tracked, and how frequently?

score_1_desc:
Order fulfillment time (order-received to ready-for-rider-handover) not measured.
No defined Service Level Agreement (SLA).
Fill rate not tracked, or under 90% where estimated.
SLA breach count not tracked.
Delayed-dispatch-from-dark-store and delayed-handover-to-customer not counted separately.
No material traceability back to the shelf a pick came from.
Breaches trigger no Root Cause Analysis (RCA) or Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA).
score_2_desc:
A fulfillment-time target exists informally, not systematically tracked.
Fill rate runs 90-95%, reviewed monthly.
Breach count known anecdotally, not tracked as delayed-dispatch vs. delayed-handover.
Traceability to shelf, where attempted, is a manual note, kept inconsistently.
RCA done occasionally after a breach.
No CAPA or closure tracking.
score_3_desc:
Fulfillment time tracked for majority of orders against a defined SLA (e.g., under 10-15 minutes).
Fill rate runs 95-97%, reviewed weekly.
SLA breach count tracked and split into delayed-dispatch-from-dark-store and delayed-handover-to-customer for majority of breaches.
Material traceability to shelf maintained via manual/physical log for majority of orders.
RCA conducted for majority of breaches.
CAPA and closure TAT applied inconsistently.
score_4_desc:
Fulfillment time tracked in real time for over 90% of orders, with automated breach alerts.
Fill rate runs 97-99%, reviewed daily with root-cause on misses.
Breach counts, split into delayed-dispatch and delayed-handover, tracked in real time.
Material traceability to shelf digitized via Quick Response (QR) code scanning for majority of orders.
Every breach triggers an RCA followed by a CAPA with a defined closure TAT, met for majority of cases.
score_5_desc:
Fulfillment time tracked in real time for 100% of orders, consistently meeting/exceeding the SLA.
Fill rate exceeds 99%, with predictive staffing adjustments during demand spikes.
Breach counts (delayed-dispatch and delayed-handover) tracked in real time, held near-zero.
Material traceability to shelf via QR-code scan covers 100% of orders.
Every breach triggers an RCA and CAPA, closure TAT met 100% of the time.
A store breaching SLAs without closing the RCA/CAPA loop cannot score here, regardless of raw SLA %.
indicative_scoring_questions:
• Is order fulfillment time (order-received to ready-for-rider-handover) tracked against a defined SLA (e.g., under 10-15 minutes), and for what % of orders?
• What is the current fill rate %?
• Is SLA breach count split between delayed-dispatch-from-dark-store and delayed-handover-to-customer?
• Is there material traceability back to the shelf a pick came from - manual log, or Quick Response (QR) code scan?
• Does every breach trigger a Root Cause Analysis (RCA) and Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) with a defined closure TAT?

score_1_desc:
No defined zones (fast-moving/slow-moving, ambient/chilled, returns) within the dark store.
SKUs placed wherever space allows.
No velocity-based (X/Y/Z) zoning - high-velocity ('X'), medium ('Y'), low-velocity ('Z') SKUs not positioned by pick frequency.
Chilled/frozen items and leafy vegetables picked in no defined sequence.
No late-pick principle to protect temperature or reduce wilting.
No container-packing sequence - heavier and fragile/light items not deliberately positioned, causing crushing damage.
Pickers routinely search multiple areas to locate a SKU.
score_2_desc:
Basic zones marked informally (hand-written signage), not consistently followed.
Zone adherence not audited.
X/Y/Z velocity classification, if it exists, not mapped to positioning.
Chilled/frozen and leafy items picked at the same point in the sequence as ambient items - no late-pick awareness.
Heavy-bottom/light-top container packing left to individual packer habit, not a defined rule.
score_3_desc:
Zones defined and mapped for majority of categories.
Velocity-based placement (fast-movers near packing) applied to some SKUs.
Zone adherence audited monthly.
X/Y/Z velocity zoning applied to some SKUs, driven by pick frequency, but not the full catalog.
Chilled/frozen items and leafy vegetables picked late in sequence for some orders, inconsistently enforced.
Heavier items placed at container bottom, fragile/light on top for some orders - not a defined Standard Operating Procedure (SOP).
score_4_desc:
Zones defined for all categories with velocity-based slotting applied to over 80% of SKUs.
Re-slotted quarterly.
Zone adherence audited weekly with corrective action on drift.
X/Y/Z zoning (high-velocity closest to packing, low-velocity furthest) covers over 80% of SKUs, positioned by pick frequency.
Chilled/frozen items and leafy vegetables sequenced as late picks for majority of orders, minimizing cold-exposure/wilting risk.
Heavy-bottom, fragile/light-top container packing followed as a defined sequence for majority of orders.
score_5_desc:
Zones and slotting continuously optimized using real-time movement/velocity data, with automated re-slotting recommendations.
Zone adherence exceeds 95%, verified via routine audit with zero unresolved drift.
X/Y/Z velocity zoning fully pick-frequency-driven and continuously re-validated - zero arbitrary placement.
Chilled/frozen items and leafy vegetables picked last in sequence for 100% of orders, zero avoidable exposure/wilting incidents.
Heavy-bottom, fragile/light-top container packing followed on 100% of orders, zero crush-damage incidents.
indicative_scoring_questions:
• Are zones defined (fast/slow-moving, ambient/chilled, returns), and are they followed and audited?
• Is X/Y/Z velocity-based zoning applied (high-velocity SKUs closest to packing), and for what % of SKUs?
• Are chilled/frozen items and leafy vegetables sequenced as late picks to reduce cold-exposure/wilting risk?
• Is there a defined container-packing sequence - heavy items at the bottom, fragile/light on top?
• How often is zone adherence audited, and is re-slotting done using real-time movement/velocity data?

score_1_desc: Shelf availability (on-shelf-in-stock %) is not measured; stockouts are identified only when a customer order fails or a rider/store staff notices; no defined replenishment trigger from the dark store to the warehouse.
score_2_desc: Shelf availability is checked manually and periodically (e.g., once a shift); replenishment requests are raised manually and irregularly; stockout duration is not tracked.
score_3_desc: Shelf availability is tracked via the inventory system for the majority of SKUs, reviewed at least twice daily; a defined reorder-point triggers a replenishment request for the majority of SKUs; stockout duration is tracked weekly.
score_4_desc: Shelf availability is tracked in real time for over 90% of SKUs with automated low-stock alerts; replenishment requests are system-generated against a min-max model for over 90% of SKUs; stockout duration is tracked daily and root-caused.
score_5_desc: Shelf availability is tracked in real time for 100% of SKUs and held above a defined benchmark (e.g., 98%+); replenishment is fully automated and demand-responsive; stockout incidents are rare, root-caused within the same day, and drive continuous reorder-point recalibration.
indicative_scoring_questions:
• Is shelf availability (on-shelf-in-stock %) tracked via the inventory system, and how often - real-time, daily, manual, or not tracked?
• Is there a defined reorder-point/min-max trigger for replenishment requests, and for what % of SKUs is it system-generated?
• Is stockout duration tracked, and is it root-caused?
• Are low-stock alerts automated?

score_1_desc:
Dark store capacity (storage positions, order-handling capacity) not documented.
No basis for knowing whether the store runs over- or under-capacity.
Overflow/congestion during peak hours common and unmanaged.
SKU mix stocked not checked against the store's demand profile.
Absolute unit count and Days of Holding (DoH) per SKU not tracked - stockout and spoilage risk for fresh produce go unmanaged.
score_2_desc:
A rough capacity estimate exists (e.g., based on floor area), not validated against actual peak order volume.
No directional over-/under-capacity flag derived - capacity status is a guess.
SKU mix not compared to the store's demand profile.
Unit count and DoH per SKU not tracked.
Overflow incidents noticed but not logged.
score_3_desc:
Rated capacity documented and compared against actual peak-hour volume at least monthly.
A directional over-/under-capacity flag, with magnitude (e.g., % above/below rated capacity), derived at least monthly.
SKU mix stocked checked against the store's demand profile for majority of SKUs.
Unit count and DoH per SKU tracked against a target band for majority of SKUs.
Overflow incidents logged, though root cause inconsistent.
score_4_desc:
Capacity utilization tracked continuously against rated capacity, peak-hour utilization consistently benchmarked.
Over-/under-capacity flag and magnitude tracked continuously, feeding new dark-store sizing/expansion decisions.
SKU mix reviewed regularly against demand profile, with corrective stocking-mix action taken.
Unit count and DoH per SKU held within target band for majority of SKUs, balancing stockout risk against spoilage risk.
Overflow incidents root-caused.
score_5_desc:
Capacity utilization tracked in real time across the dark-store network, with predictive flagging of stores approaching capacity constraints ahead of peak demand.
Over-/under-capacity flag and magnitude tracked in real time, systematically informing sizing decisions for new/expanding stores.
SKU mix continuously matched to each store's demand profile.
Unit count and DoH per SKU maintained within target band for effectively all SKUs, keeping stockout and spoilage risk both in check.
Zero unplanned overflow incidents.
indicative_scoring_questions:
• Is dark store capacity (storage positions, order-handling capacity) documented and compared against actual peak-hour volume?
• Is a directional over-/under-capacity flag with magnitude derived, and how often?
• Is SKU mix checked against the store's demand profile?
• Are unit count and Days of Holding (DoH) per SKU tracked against a target band?
• Are overflow incidents logged and root-caused?

score_1_desc: Dark-store replenishment quantities are decided independently of the demand forecast (e.g., based on a store manager's ad hoc request); the forecast, even where it exists (A13.1), does not feed the replenishment process.
score_2_desc: The forecast informs replenishment for some high-velocity SKUs only, applied inconsistently; the majority of replenishment decisions still rely on manual judgment or store requests.
score_3_desc: The forecast feeds replenishment quantity calculation for the majority of SKUs via a defined formula (e.g., forecast demand plus safety stock minus current inventory), reviewed periodically for linkage accuracy.
score_4_desc: The forecast-driven replenishment formula covers over 90% of SKUs, with linkage accuracy tracked weekly and manual override rate held under a defined benchmark.
score_5_desc: Replenishment quantities are forecast-driven for 100% of SKUs with automated recalculation as the forecast updates, manual overrides rare and logged with reason, and linkage accuracy tracked in real time.
indicative_scoring_questions:
• Does the demand forecast feed dark-store replenishment quantities, or are quantities decided independently (e.g., a store manager's ad hoc request)?
• What % of SKUs have replenishment quantities derived via a defined formula (forecast demand plus safety stock minus current inventory)?
• Is linkage accuracy between forecast and replenishment tracked, and how often?
• What is the manual override rate, and is it held under a defined benchmark?

score_1_desc: Replenishment frequency to dark stores is irregular (less than once daily on average) and not planned against SKU velocity or shelf life; fill rate is not tracked at the dark-store level.
score_2_desc: A nominal replenishment frequency exists (e.g., once daily) but is not consistently met; fill rate is checked only when a stockout is escalated.
score_3_desc: Replenishment frequency is defined and met for the majority of dark stores/days, with fill rate tracked weekly at the dark-store level.
score_4_desc: Replenishment frequency is tuned by SKU velocity/shelf life for the majority of SKUs, with fill rate tracked daily per dark store and held above a defined benchmark.
score_5_desc: Replenishment frequency is dynamically tuned by real-time velocity, shelf-life, and dark-store inventory position; fill rate is tracked in real time per dark store per SKU and consistently exceeds a defined benchmark (e.g., 97%+).
indicative_scoring_questions:
• What is the replenishment frequency to dark stores (cycles/day), and is it planned against SKU velocity/shelf life?
• Is fill rate tracked at the dark-store level, and how often - real-time, daily, weekly, or only on escalation?
• Is replenishment frequency dynamically tuned by real-time velocity, shelf-life, and dark-store inventory position?
• Does fill rate consistently exceed a defined benchmark (e.g., 97%+)?

score_1_desc:
Stock-out rate (% of SKUs out of stock at the dark store) not tracked - discovered only via lost-sale complaints.
Excess-inventory rate (% of SKUs holding above target Days of Inventory (DoI)/Days of Holding (DoH)) not tracked - discovered only via physical overflow or wastage.
score_2_desc:
Stock-out rate tracked only when a stockout escalates to a complaint - no routine measurement.
Excess-inventory rate not tracked at the dark-store level; resulting wastage not systematically linked back to excess DoI/DoH.
score_3_desc:
Stock-out rate tracked weekly at the dark-store level for majority of SKUs, against a defined target band.
Excess-inventory rate tracked weekly at the dark-store level for majority of SKUs, against a target DoI/DoH band.
Emergency replenishment trips logged.
score_4_desc:
Stock-out rate tracked daily per dark store per SKU, root-caused (forecast error, replenishment frequency, or shelf-life) for over 90% of incidents, lost-sales impact quantified.
Excess-inventory rate tracked daily per dark store per SKU against the target DoI/DoH band, root-caused for over 90% of incidents, resulting wastage quantified.
score_5_desc:
Stock-out rate tracked in real time per SKU, held within a tight target band, root-caused same-day.
Excess-inventory rate tracked in real time per SKU against the target DoI/DoH band, held within a tight range, root-caused same-day.
Trade-off between stock-out risk and excess-driven wastage is actively and continuously optimized across the dark-store network.
indicative_scoring_questions:
• Is stock-out rate tracked routinely at the dark-store/SKU level, or only discovered via lost-sale complaints?
• Is excess-inventory rate tracked against a target Days of Inventory (DoI)/Days of Holding (DoH) band?
• Are stockout and excess-inventory incidents root-caused (forecast error, replenishment frequency, or shelf-life), and how quickly?
• Is resulting wastage from excess inventory quantified?
• Is the stock-out-versus-excess trade-off actively optimized across the dark-store network?

score_1_desc: No defined fleet plan (dry/reefer vehicle count) against dispatch volume; vehicle shortages and last-minute market/spot-hire are frequent (over 20% of trips); no backup-fleet arrangement exists.
score_2_desc: A fleet count exists informally, but shortages leading to spot-hire occur on 10-20% of trips; backup fleet is arranged ad hoc, after a shortage is already identified.
score_3_desc: Fleet size is documented against average daily dispatch volume, reviewed monthly; spot-hire/backup usage is held under 10% of trips; a defined backup-fleet vendor exists and is engaged before the shortfall causes a missed dispatch.
score_4_desc: Fleet size is reviewed against both average and peak dispatch volume, with dedicated and backup fleet contracted in advance; spot-hire usage is under 5% of trips, tracked and root-caused monthly.
score_5_desc: Fleet planning is dynamically adjusted to forecast dispatch volume (including seasonal/event peaks) with a pre-qualified backup pool on standby; spot-hire/placement-failure trips are under 1%, tracked in real time with root-cause closed within the week.
indicative_scoring_questions:
• Is fleet size (dry/reefer vehicle count) documented against dispatch volume, and reviewed against both average and peak volume?
• What % of trips require spot-hire/market vehicles due to shortage?
• Is a backup-fleet vendor arranged in advance, or only ad hoc after a shortage occurs?
• Is fleet planning dynamically adjusted to forecast dispatch volume, including seasonal/event peaks?
• Are spot-hire/placement-failure trips root-caused, and how quickly is the root cause closed?

score_1_desc:
Vehicle utilization not measured.
Vehicles dispatched regardless of fill level.
Crate-loaded utilization (crates actually loaded vs. rated crate capacity of the vehicle) not tracked.
Empty-running and partial-load trips common and unquantified.
score_2_desc:
Utilization estimated occasionally (visual check), not systematically logged - by cube/weight or crate count.
Crate-loaded utilization not calculated against rated crate capacity - loading decisions made by eye.
Partial-load trips not tracked as a distinct metric.
score_3_desc:
Utilization tracked for majority of trips via crate count or manifest weight against a target, reviewed weekly.
Crate-loaded utilization (crates loaded / rated crate capacity) tracked alongside cube/weight utilization for majority of trips.
Partial-load trip % tracked monthly.
score_4_desc:
Utilization tracked per trip in real time for over 90% of dispatches.
Route/load consolidation applied to reduce partial loads.
Crate-loaded utilization tracked per trip alongside cube/weight utilization, both consistently at or above a defined benchmark.
score_5_desc:
Utilization optimized dynamically (load-building/route consolidation software) across the network in real time.
Crate-loaded utilization and cube/weight utilization both tracked per trip, consistently exceeding benchmark.
Empty-running held to a documented minimum.
indicative_scoring_questions:
• Is vehicle utilization measured (cube/weight or crate count), or are vehicles dispatched regardless of fill level?
• What is current crate-loaded utilization (crates loaded versus rated crate capacity)?
• Is utilization tracked per trip in real time, or only estimated/aggregated periodically?
• Is route/load consolidation applied to reduce partial loads and empty-running?

score_1_desc: On-time arrival/departure is not tracked; route adherence is not monitored; vehicle breakdown/trip cancellation is not logged as a distinct metric.
score_2_desc: On-time performance is reviewed informally/anecdotally; breakdowns and cancellations are known to staff but not consolidated into a report.
score_3_desc: On-Time Departure (OTD) and On-Time Arrival (OTA) are tracked for the majority of trips against a defined window, reviewed weekly; breakdown/cancellation rate is tracked monthly.
score_4_desc: OTD/OTA are tracked in real time (Global Positioning System-based) for over 90% of trips with automated delay alerts; breakdown/cancellation rate is held under a defined benchmark, root-caused monthly.
score_5_desc: OTD/OTA are tracked in real time across 100% of trips and consistently exceed benchmark (e.g., 95%+); breakdowns/cancellations are rare and root-caused within 24 hours, feeding preventive fleet-maintenance planning.
indicative_scoring_questions:
• Are On-Time Departure (OTD) and On-Time Arrival (OTA) tracked, and for what % of trips?
• Is tracking Global Positioning System (GPS)-based/real-time, or manual and anecdotal?
• What is the current breakdown/cancellation rate, and is it root-caused?
• Do OTD/OTA consistently exceed a defined benchmark (e.g., 95%+)?
• Does breakdown/cancellation root-causing feed preventive fleet-maintenance planning?

score_1_desc:
Transportation cost tracked only in aggregate (total monthly spend).
Cost per trip/km/unit not calculated.
Dry and reefer costs not tracked separately.
No defined Warehouse-to-Dark-Store network/route plan - routes run ad hoc with no route-optimization logic behind the cost incurred.
score_2_desc:
Cost per trip calculated periodically (monthly), not benchmarked or trended.
Dry/reefer cost split estimated, not measured.
A route plan, if it exists, is informal, not evaluated for cost or time efficiency.
score_3_desc:
Cost per trip, per km, and per unit dispatched tracked monthly, separately for dry and reefer fleet, compared against a budget.
A basic Warehouse-to-Dark-Store route plan exists, covering majority of routes, not yet formally optimized for cost and time together.
score_4_desc:
Cost metrics tracked weekly with variance-to-budget root-caused.
Cost per dark store also tracked to identify high-cost routes/stores.
Warehouse-to-Dark-Store network plan reviewed periodically and used to explain cost variance by route - not yet the primary driver of route design.
score_5_desc:
Cost metrics tracked in real time/daily, benchmarked across routes and dark stores, with a documented downward cost trend.
Cost efficiency driven by a defined, documented Warehouse-to-Dark-Store network plan that optimizes routes for both cost and time.
Low cost achieved by design, not chance; the plan directly informs route/network redesign decisions.
indicative_scoring_questions:
• Is transportation cost tracked only in aggregate, or broken down per trip, per km, and per unit?
• Are dry and reefer costs tracked separately?
• Is cost tracked per dark store to identify high-cost routes/stores?
• Is there a documented Warehouse-to-Dark-Store network/route plan optimized for both cost and time?
• Is there a documented downward cost trend, and does the network plan actively drive route/network redesign decisions?

score_1_desc:
Reefer vehicles not temperature-logged during transit.
Pre-cooling before loading not practiced or verified.
Temperature excursions identified only if product is visibly spoiled on arrival.
No digital log exists; nothing transmitted to the Control Tower team.
score_2_desc:
Temperature spot-checked manually at departure and/or arrival only.
Pre-cooling practiced inconsistently.
Excursions not systematically logged.
Where a log exists it is paper/local, not digital, and not shared with the Control Tower team.
score_3_desc:
Temperature logged (manually or via a basic logger) for majority of reefer trips, reviewed daily.
Pre-cooling before loading standard practice for majority of trips.
Logging digitized for majority of trips, but reviewed only after the trip - not transmitted live to the Control Tower team.
score_4_desc:
Temperature logged continuously via sensors for over 90% of reefer trips, with daily breach review.
Pre-cooling compliance tracked and held above a defined benchmark.
Digital temperature logs transmitted to the Control Tower team for majority of trips, though not fully live/real-time.
score_5_desc:
Temperature logged continuously via sensors for 100% of reefer trips, with real-time breach alerts and automated escalation.
Pre-cooling compliance exceeds a defined benchmark (e.g., 98%+); reefer downtime/fuel performance also tracked and trended.
Digital temperature logs transmitted live to the Control Tower team for 100% of trips, enabling real-time in-transit intervention.
indicative_scoring_questions:
• Are reefer vehicles temperature-logged during transit - manually, via basic logger, or continuous sensors?
• What % of reefer trips have continuous sensor-based temperature logging?
• Is pre-cooling before loading practiced and tracked, and at what compliance rate?
• Are temperature excursions/breaches auto-alerted in real time, or only discovered if product arrives spoiled?
• Are digital temperature logs transmitted live to the Control Tower team?

score_1_desc:
Dispatch happens as a single unplanned wave (or ad hoc multiple waves), no defined volume split or rationale.
Wave timing not documented.
Where any logic exists, wave timing is set purely by warehouse processing convenience, not dark-store demand.
score_2_desc:
A wave structure exists informally (e.g., 'morning and night'), volume split not measured against a plan.
Wave timing drifts day to day.
Wave timing defaults to warehouse readiness/convenience; dark-store demand signals are not a factor in scheduling.
score_3_desc:
A defined wave architecture (number of waves, planned volume split, cutoff times) documented and followed on majority of days, reviewed monthly.
Wave timing is intended to follow dark-store demand signals, but warehouse processing bottlenecks still frequently override the schedule by default.
score_4_desc:
Wave architecture tracked daily against plan (actual vs. planned volume split, cutoff adherence), variance root-caused weekly.
Dedicated reefer/cold-chain wave exists where applicable.
Wave timing is primarily driven by dark-store demand signals; warehouse readiness is a secondary gate, delaying a wave only as a tracked exception.
score_5_desc:
Wave architecture dynamically reviewed against demand patterns and dark-store inventory positions, adjusted on a defined cadence (e.g., monthly or faster).
Cutoff adherence exceeds a defined benchmark (e.g., 95%+), tracked in real time.
Wave timing is fully demand-driven; warehouse processing bottlenecks influence timing only as an exception input, never the primary driver.
indicative_scoring_questions:
• Is there a defined wave architecture (number of waves, planned volume split, cutoff times), documented and followed?
• Is wave timing primarily driven by dark-store demand signals, or by warehouse processing convenience/readiness?
• Is a dedicated reefer/cold-chain wave in place where applicable?
• Is actual-versus-planned volume split tracked daily, with variance root-caused?
• Does cutoff adherence exceed a defined benchmark (e.g., 95%+), tracked in real time?

score_1_desc:
Wave readiness (processing complete, picking complete, staging complete, dock and manpower available) not tracked as a combined checkpoint.
Waves routinely depart late due to one or more of these not being ready.
Vehicles are placed on a fixed clock regardless of whether material is processed, packed, and allocated.
score_2_desc:
Readiness checked informally by a supervisor shortly before cutoff.
Late departures due to readiness gaps known anecdotally, not logged by cause.
Vehicle placement still follows a fixed schedule; material-readiness state is not a placement condition.
score_3_desc:
A defined readiness checklist (processing/picking/staging/dock/manpower) checked before each wave for majority of waves, late-departure cause logged.
Vehicle placement linked to confirmed processing, packing, and allocation status for majority of waves.
A fixed-clock fallback is still used when this check is skipped.
score_4_desc:
Readiness tracked systematically for over 90% of waves with a live pre-cutoff dashboard.
Late-departure root causes reviewed weekly and closed.
A vehicle is placed for a wave only once material is confirmed processed, packed, and allocated, for over 90% of waves - not on a fixed clock.
score_5_desc:
Readiness tracked in real time with predictive flagging of at-risk waves well before cutoff, allowing pre-emptive corrective action.
On-time wave departure exceeds a defined benchmark (e.g., 98%+).
Vehicle placement is gated 100% of the time on confirmed processed-packed-allocated material status - zero clock-driven placements ahead of material readiness.
indicative_scoring_questions:
• Is a combined readiness checkpoint (processing, picking, staging, dock, manpower) checked before each wave?
• Is vehicle placement gated on confirmed processed/packed/allocated material status, or placed on a fixed clock regardless of readiness?
• What % of waves have readiness tracked systematically via a dashboard, versus checked informally by a supervisor?
• Are late-departure causes logged and root-caused?
• Is there predictive flagging of at-risk waves well ahead of cutoff?

score_1_desc:
Wave volumes and SKU mix not aligned to dark-store demand/inventory position.
Stock-outs at the dark store before the next wave arrives are common and untracked as a wave-design issue.
Overstocking/excess inventory at the dark store right after a wave lands is equally common and untracked.
score_2_desc:
Misalignment noticed reactively via complaints, not measured systematically.
Pre-next-wave stock-outs known anecdotally, not logged.
Post-wave overstock/excess known anecdotally, not logged.
score_3_desc:
Wave volume/SKU mix checked against dark-store inventory position for majority of waves before dispatch, misalignment incidents logged monthly.
Stock-out incidence between waves logged for majority of dark stores.
Overstock/excess-inventory incidence immediately after a wave lands logged for majority of dark stores.
score_4_desc:
Wave planning incorporates dark-store inventory position, SKU velocity, and shelf-life systematically for over 90% of waves.
Emergency/off-cycle trips tracked and root-caused.
Pre-next-wave stock-out incidence tracked and root-caused for over 90% of dark stores.
Post-wave overstock/excess incidence tracked and root-caused for over 90% of dark stores.
score_5_desc:
Wave planning dynamically driven by real-time dark-store inventory and demand signals, minimizing both under- and over-replenishment.
Emergency trips rare and root-caused, with continuous tuning of the wave-to-demand model.
Stock-outs between waves held near-zero across the network, tracked in real time.
Overstock/excess inventory immediately after a wave lands held near-zero across the network, tracked in real time.
indicative_scoring_questions:
• Is wave volume/SKU mix checked against dark-store inventory position before dispatch?
• Are stock-outs between waves (before the next wave arrives) tracked and root-caused?
• Is post-wave overstock/excess inventory at the dark store tracked and root-caused?
• Does wave planning incorporate dark-store inventory position, SKU velocity, and shelf-life systematically?
• Are emergency/off-cycle trips tracked, and are they rare and root-caused?

score_1_desc:
No consolidated inbound view exists.
Visibility limited to yard walks and calls to supervisors.
None of the following tracked against target:
Inbound Turnaround Time (TAT), scheduled-vs-actual arrival, scheduled-vs-actual delivery, vendor scorecards, Quality Check (QC) processing status, rejection tracking, on-hold time, cost.
Deviations not escalated to management.
score_2_desc:
A few of the 8 data points tracked in a system.
Coverage under 40% of TAT, arrival, delivery, vendor scorecard, QC status, rejection, on-hold time, and cost.
No target-vs-actual comparison for most metrics.
Deviations reviewed only after escalation, not proactively.
score_3_desc:
Consolidated dashboard covers 40-75% of the 8 data points.
TAT, arrival, and delivery tracked against target.
QC status and rejections visible but refreshed hourly, not live.
Deviations reviewed once per shift; escalation inconsistent.
score_4_desc:
Consolidated dashboard covers over 75% of the 8 data points.
TAT, arrival, delivery, QC, rejection, on-hold time, and cost tracked against target.
Vendor scorecards used routinely in decisions.
Deviations auto-flagged and escalated to management same shift.
score_5_desc:
Real-time dashboard covers 100% of the 8 data points, each tracked against target:
TAT, scheduled-vs-actual arrival, scheduled-vs-actual delivery, vendor scorecards, QC status, rejection tracking, on-hold time, cost.
Deviations auto-escalated to management in real time.
Zero data points tracked manually or off-system.
indicative_scoring_questions:
• How many of the 8 inbound data points (Turnaround Time (TAT), scheduled-vs-actual arrival, scheduled-vs-actual delivery, vendor scorecards, Quality Check (QC) status, rejection tracking, on-hold time, cost) are tracked in a single consolidated view?
• Is the dashboard refreshed live/real-time, or only hourly or periodically?
• Are vendor scorecards used routinely in decisions?
• Are deviations auto-flagged and escalated to management, or only reviewed after a complaint/escalation?

score_1_desc:
Processing progress not visible outside the floor.
Sorting & Grading (S&G) progress vs. plan not tracked.
Packing progress vs. plan not tracked.
Shortfalls not linked to dispatch risk.
Processing cost not tracked.
Productivity known only at end of shift, if at all.
score_2_desc:
S&G and packing progress tracked manually, end-of-shift only.
Shortfall not flagged as a dispatch risk during the shift.
Cost tracking absent or reviewed monthly only.
Productivity numbers compiled after shift, not live.
score_3_desc:
S&G and packing progress vs. plan visible at set checkpoints (e.g., every 2 hours).
Shortfall reviewed by supervisor, not auto-linked to dispatch risk.
Processing cost tracked at shift level.
Productivity numbers available with a lag, not live.
score_4_desc:
S&G and packing progress vs. plan tracked near-real-time for over 90% of volume.
Shortfall automatically flagged as a dispatch-risk signal.
Processing cost tracked and reviewed daily.
Live productivity numbers available per stage during the shift.
score_5_desc:
S&G and packing progress vs. plan tracked in real time for 100% of volume.
Any shortfall auto-triggers a dispatch-risk alert same shift.
Processing cost tracked in real time against target.
Live productivity numbers visible per stage, refreshed continuously, not just at shift-end.
indicative_scoring_questions:
• Is Sorting & Grading (S&G) and packing progress tracked against plan, and how frequently - real-time, fixed checkpoints, or end-of-shift only?
• Is a processing shortfall automatically linked to dispatch risk, or only reviewed by a supervisor after the fact?
• Is processing cost tracked in real time against target, or only at shift/monthly level?
• Are live productivity numbers available per processing stage during the shift?

score_1_desc:

Overrides require supervisor approval for the majority of transaction types.
System-logged reason captured for the majority of overrides.

Role-based access control defined for key roles.
Approval flow reflects the organization's hierarchy for most transaction types.

Overrides require system-enforced approval workflows for over 90% of transaction types.
Every transaction tied to a named user and timestamp for over 90% of transactions.

Inbound and outbound traceability system-linked for over 90% of transactions.

Operator-wait incidents rare, root-caused within the week; emergency rental a planned contingency.
indicative_scoring_questions:
• Is Material Handling Equipment (MHE) fleet count/type benchmarked against a defined industry standard and peak-hour (not just average) volume?
• Is charging-station count checked against fleet size, and are wait-for-charger incidents tracked?
• Is there a dedicated, maintained MHE storage/parking area?
• Are operator wait-for-equipment incidents tracked weekly and root-caused?
• Is equipment shortage handled reactively (emergency rental after a slowdown) or via a pre-arranged backup plan?

score_1_desc:
Equipment utilization, breakdown frequency, battery-charging patterns not tracked.
Preventive Maintenance (PM) reactive (fix-on-failure only); no PM schedule exists.
Battery/equipment performance not benchmarked against any defined industry standard.
score_2_desc:
Breakdowns logged in a register; Mean Time Between Failures (MTBF)/Mean Time To Repair (MTTR) not calculated.
A PM schedule exists on paper but not consistently followed; adherence unmeasured.
Battery charging follows no defined rotation; performance untracked.
score_3_desc:
Utilization and breakdown frequency tracked monthly.
PM schedule followed for the majority of equipment.
PM adherence tracked against a defined industry-standard cadence.
Battery charging follows a basic rotation but is not optimized.
score_4_desc:
Utilization, MTBF, MTTR tracked weekly per equipment unit.
PM compliance tracked, held above benchmark, aligned to a defined industry-standard cadence.
Battery management (charge scheduling, swap availability) planned to avoid mid-shift downtime.
Battery performance tracked against the PM schedule.
score_5_desc:
Utilization, MTBF, MTTR tracked in real time (telematics-enabled where applicable) per unit.
Drives a predictive maintenance program benchmarked against the defined industry-standard PM cadence.
PM adherence at or above benchmark, zero missed cycles.
Battery management fully scheduled, zero mid-shift charging-related downtime.
Battery performance tracked and trended continuously.
indicative_scoring_questions:
• Is Preventive Maintenance (PM) scheduled and followed, or reactive fix-on-failure only? What is current PM adherence %?
• Are Mean Time Between Failures (MTBF) and Mean Time To Repair (MTTR) calculated, and how often is utilization/breakdown tracked (never / monthly / weekly / real time)?
• Is the PM cadence benchmarked against a defined industry standard?
• How is battery charging managed - no rotation, basic rotation, or scheduled to avoid mid-shift downtime?
• Is there a telematics-enabled predictive maintenance program?

score_1_desc: Internal material movement (travel distance, backtracking, cross-movement, double handling) is not measured; congestion and pedestrian/MHE conflict points are known anecdotally but not mapped.
score_2_desc: Movement inefficiencies are noticed by supervisors but not quantified; no one-way flow or designated pedestrian/MHE lanes exist in congested areas.
score_3_desc: A basic flow map exists identifying major backtracking/cross-movement points, reviewed periodically; one-way flow and pedestrian/MHE segregation are implemented in the highest-risk areas.
score_4_desc: Travel distance and double-handling incidence are sampled/measured periodically (e.g., quarterly time-motion study) and used to adjust slotting or flow; congestion points are tracked and reduced measurably year-on-year.
score_5_desc: Travel distance and double-handling are tracked continuously (e.g., via WMS travel-path data) and used to drive ongoing slotting and flow optimization; pedestrian/MHE conflict points are eliminated or fully controlled, with a documented downward trend in average travel distance.
indicative_scoring_questions:
• Is travel distance, backtracking, cross-movement, or double handling measured, or only known anecdotally?
• Does a current flow map exist identifying major backtracking/cross-movement/congestion points?
• Are one-way flow and pedestrian/MHE segregation implemented in the highest-risk areas?
• Is travel distance/double handling sampled periodically (e.g., a time-motion study) or tracked continuously via WMS travel-path data?
• Is there a documented, sustained downward trend in average travel distance?

score_1_desc: Products requiring 0-4C storage (cut produce, exotic produce, chilled Food & Beverage (F&B) items) are stored without a documented temperature map or defined dwell-time limit; door-opening frequency is not managed; incompatible products are stored together.
score_2_desc: A chiller exists and is used for the intended products, but temperature mapping, dwell-time limits, and product segregation are not formally defined or monitored.
score_3_desc: Temperature is logged (manual or basic logger) for the majority of chiller zones, reviewed daily; product segregation and a basic dwell-time expectation are defined and followed for the majority of SKUs.
score_4_desc: Temperature is logged continuously via sensors for over 90% of chiller zones with daily excursion review; dwell time and door-opening frequency are monitored and held within defined limits for the majority of product categories.
score_5_desc: Temperature is logged continuously via sensors across 100% of chiller zones with real-time excursion alerts and automated escalation; dwell time, door-opening, and product segregation are all actively managed and audited, with backup refrigeration verified and tested on a defined schedule.
indicative_scoring_questions:
• Is there a documented temperature map and defined dwell-time limit for 0-4C chiller zones?
• What % of chiller zones have continuous sensor-based logging vs. manual logger vs. none?
• Are incompatible products segregated within the chiller, and is door-opening frequency managed?
• Are temperature excursions reviewed daily, or alerted and escalated in real time?
• Is backup refrigeration verified and tested on a defined schedule?

score_1_desc:
Leafy produce received, sorted, graded, packed at ambient temperature.
No defined time-outside-controlled-temperature limit.
Storage/processing temperature range (15-20C) not defined or enforced.
No handling norms (stacking, transfer time, ethylene co-location) defined.
Damage/shelf-life impact from heat exposure not tracked.
score_2_desc:
A 15-20C storage/processing intent exists, not consistently enforced.
Leafy product frequently sits at ambient temperature between receiving and cold processing, no tracked time limit.
Basic handling norms known informally, not standardized.
score_3_desc:
Time-outside-controlled-temperature tracked for the majority of batches against an informal target.
The 15-20C band maintained for most storage/processing steps.
Handling norms (stacking limits, transfer-time limits, ethylene segregation) defined, followed inconsistently.
Damage attributable to heat exposure logged when identified.
score_4_desc:
Time-outside-controlled-temperature tracked for over 90% of batches against a defined target, damage reviewed weekly, root-caused.
The 15-20C band maintained continuously through storage/processing for most batches.
Handling norms (no crushing stacks, minimal ambient exposure in transfers, ethylene segregation) followed for most batches.
score_5_desc:
Time-outside-controlled-temperature tracked in real time for 100% of batches, held within a benchmark-tight window, receiving through dispatch.
The 15-20C band maintained continuously, receiving through dispatch, zero unmanaged lapses.
Handling norms fully enforced: no crushing stacks, no prolonged ambient exposure, no ethylene co-location.
Damage/shelf-life impact at or below a defined minimum, continuously monitored.
indicative_scoring_questions:
• Is leafy produce held continuously within the 15-20C band from receiving to dispatch, or does it sit at ambient temperature between steps?
• Is time-outside-controlled-temperature tracked per batch, against what target, and for what % of batches?
• Are handling norms (stacking limits, transfer-time limits, no ethylene co-location) defined and actually followed?
• Is damage/shelf-life impact from heat exposure logged and root-caused weekly?

score_1_desc:
Hydroponic produce handled with no protocol distinct from standard field-grown leafy.
Despite higher moisture content and fragility.
Storage/processing temperature range (15-20C) not specifically enforced.
No hydroponics-specific handling norms (extra care against crushing, shorter ambient tolerance, no ethylene co-location) defined.
Damage/quality issues from mishandling not tracked separately from standard leafy.
score_2_desc:
A distinct handling intent for hydroponic produce exists, not formalized or consistently followed.
15-20C band targeted, not tracked separately from general leafy.
Hydroponics-specific norms (tighter stacking, shorter transfer-time tolerance) known informally, not standardized.
Damage from hydroponics-specific mishandling not isolated in quality data.
score_3_desc:
A defined handling/temperature protocol exists, followed for the majority of batches.
15-20C band maintained for most storage/processing steps.
Tighter stacking and transfer-time limits than standard leafy, given higher moisture/fragility.
Damage/rejection from temperature or handling tracked separately, reviewed periodically.
score_4_desc:
Protocol followed for over 90% of batches, staging and dispatch handling also covered.
15-20C band maintained continuously for most batches.
Stricter stacking/transfer-time discipline than standard leafy.
No co-location with ethylene-releasing produce for most batches.
Damage/rejection from hydroponics handling tracked weekly, held under a defined benchmark.
score_5_desc:
Protocol followed for 100% of batches end-to-end, receiving through dispatch staging.
15-20C band maintained continuously, zero unmanaged lapses.
Reflects the tighter handling care hydroponic product needs vs. regular field-grown leafy.
Zero crushing stacks, zero prolonged ambient exposure, zero ethylene co-location.
Damage/rejection from temperature or handling at or near zero, continuously monitored.
indicative_scoring_questions:
• Does hydroponic produce get a handling protocol distinct from standard field-grown leafy, given its higher moisture and fragility?
• Is the 15-20C band and time-outside-controlled-temperature tracked separately for hydroponics, not lumped with general leafy?
• Are tighter stacking and shorter transfer-time limits enforced than for standard leafy?
• Is hydroponics-specific damage/rejection tracked separately, and what % is attributable to temperature or handling?
• Is co-location with ethylene-releasing produce avoided?

score_1_desc: Temperature continuity from inbound verification through dispatch is not tracked as an end-to-end chain; each stage is managed independently with no visibility into where the cold chain is broken.
score_2_desc: Temperature is checked at 1-2 points in the chain (e.g., inbound gate and cold storage) but not at intermediate stages (processing, staging); breaks in continuity are not identified.
score_3_desc: Temperature is checked at the majority of chain stages for the majority of cold-chain SKUs, with an informal understanding of where breaks are most likely; reviewed periodically.
score_4_desc: Temperature continuity is tracked across over 90% of chain stages for cold-chain SKUs, with breaks (door-opening, staging delay, ante-room transit) flagged and reviewed weekly.
score_5_desc: Temperature continuity is tracked and verified at every chain stage in real time for 100% of cold-chain SKUs, with zero unmanaged breaks and automated escalation the moment a break occurs, including at reefer vehicle handover.
indicative_scoring_questions:
• Is temperature continuity tracked as one end-to-end chain from inbound verification through dispatch, or is each stage managed independently with no visibility into breaks?
• At which chain stages is temperature actually checked - just inbound gate, or also processing, staging, and reefer-vehicle handover?
• What % of chain stages/cold-chain SKUs maintain the required temperature band?
• Are breaks (door-opening, staging delay, ante-room transit, reefer handover) flagged, reviewed, and auto-escalated?

score_1_desc: Refrigeration reliability (breakdown frequency, backup refrigeration availability, alarm response) is not tracked; a refrigeration failure is discovered only when product temperature has already been compromised.
score_2_desc: Breakdowns are logged when they occur, but uptime %, backup refrigeration testing, and alarm-response time are not measured.
score_3_desc: Refrigeration uptime is tracked monthly; backup refrigeration exists and is tested periodically; alarms exist but response time is not measured.
score_4_desc: Refrigeration uptime is tracked weekly and held above a defined benchmark; backup refrigeration is tested on a defined schedule; alarm response time is tracked and held under a defined target.
score_5_desc: Refrigeration uptime is tracked continuously and held above a defined benchmark (e.g., 99%+); backup refrigeration is tested and proven on a defined schedule with zero unplanned cold-chain downtime; alarms trigger automated escalation with response time consistently under a defined target.
indicative_scoring_questions:
• Is refrigeration uptime tracked, at what frequency (not tracked / monthly / weekly / continuously), and what is the current uptime %?
• Does backup refrigeration exist, and is it tested on a defined schedule?
• Are alarms in place, and is alarm response time measured and held under a target?
• Is a refrigeration failure typically caught by monitoring, or only discovered after product temperature is already compromised?

area_name: Food & Beverage (F&B) / Non-Goods and Services Tax (Non-GST) Operating Segregation
score_1_desc: Products treated as Food & Beverage (F&B)/Non-Goods and Services Tax (Non-GST) (e.g., fresh produce, milk, curd, other exempt dairy) share storage and processing space with other inventory with no physical demarcation; there is no documented list of which products are treated this way.
score_2_desc: A list of applicable products exists, but physical segregation in storage/processing is informal and not consistently maintained; movement between segregated and non-segregated areas is not controlled.
score_3_desc: Defined storage/processing zones exist for F&B/Non-GST products and are followed for the majority of applicable SKUs, audited periodically; movement control exists but relies on manual discipline.
score_4_desc: Segregation is maintained for over 90% of applicable SKUs with zone access/movement controlled (e.g., physical barriers, defined transfer points), audited monthly with corrective action on drift.
score_5_desc: Segregation is maintained for 100% of applicable SKUs with system-enforced movement control (e.g., WMS location-type restrictions) and zero unresolved audit findings, sustained over consecutive audit cycles.
indicative_scoring_questions:
• Is there a documented list of which products are treated as Food & Beverage (F&B)/Non-Goods and Services Tax (Non-GST) (e.g., fresh produce, milk, curd, exempt dairy)?
• Are these products physically segregated in storage/processing with defined zones, and what % of applicable SKUs is covered?
• Is movement between segregated and non-segregated areas controlled, and is it audited?
• Is movement control system-enforced (e.g., WMS location-type restrictions) or reliant on manual discipline?

area_name: Food & Beverage (F&B) / Non-Goods and Services Tax (Non-GST) Operating Segregation
score_1_desc: The WMS does not distinguish F&B/Non-GST inventory from other stock; ownership and documentation for these products follow the same process as all other inventory, with no distinct traceability.
score_2_desc: A manual register or spreadsheet tracks F&B/Non-GST inventory separately, but the WMS itself does not tag or segregate it; reconciliation between the register and the WMS is manual and infrequent.
score_3_desc: The WMS tags the majority of applicable SKUs with a distinct location/inventory type, with documentation (billing flow, ownership records) maintained separately and reconciled periodically.
score_4_desc: The WMS tags over 90% of applicable SKUs with system-enforced segregation, with documentation and billing flow reconciled monthly with zero unresolved discrepancies.
score_5_desc: The WMS fully segregates 100% of applicable SKUs with system-enforced controls, complete traceability, and documentation reconciled in real time with zero discrepancies, sustained over consecutive review cycles.
indicative_scoring_questions:
• Does the WMS tag F&B/Non-GST inventory with a distinct location/inventory type, or is it tracked only on a manual register/spreadsheet?
• What % of applicable SKUs are system-tagged for segregation?
• Are documentation and billing flow reconciled against the WMS, and how often (infrequent manual vs. monthly vs. real time)?
• Are there unresolved discrepancies between the register/WMS and actual ownership records?

area_name: Food & Beverage (F&B) / Non-Goods and Services Tax (Non-GST) Operating Segregation
score_1_desc: There is no awareness at the operational level of why F&B/Non-GST products are (or should be) segregated; inconsistent physical/system segregation creates a visible audit/compliance risk that has not been assessed by a tax or compliance specialist.
score_2_desc: Operational staff are aware segregation matters but have not been briefed on the specific compliance requirement; no periodic internal audit checks segregation compliance risk.
score_3_desc: Operational staff are briefed on the segregation requirement and a periodic internal audit checks physical/system/documentation consistency; findings are logged, though closure is inconsistent.
score_4_desc: Segregation compliance risk is audited on a defined schedule (e.g., quarterly) with findings closed within a defined SLA; the operational team maintains a working relationship with a tax/compliance function to flag ambiguous cases.
score_5_desc: Segregation compliance risk is audited on a defined schedule with a sustained zero-unresolved-finding record; any ambiguous product/process scenario is proactively escalated to and validated by a Goods and Services Tax (GST)/Tax specialist before it becomes an operational practice, with that validation documented and retained.
indicative_scoring_questions:
• Are operational staff briefed on why F&B/Non-GST segregation matters, or just aware it matters without knowing the requirement?
• Is there a periodic internal audit checking physical/system/documentation consistency for this segregation risk?
• Are audit findings logged and closed within a defined Service Level Agreement (SLA)?
• Is there a working relationship with a Goods and Services Tax (GST)/tax specialist to flag and validate ambiguous scenarios before they become practice?

score_1_desc: There is no current process-flow map of the facility; backtracking, cross-movement between raw and processed material, and MHE/pedestrian conflict points are not identified.
score_2_desc: A process-flow map was created at some point (e.g., at facility setup) but is outdated and not revisited as operations changed; known congestion points are managed informally.
score_3_desc: A current process-flow map exists, reviewed periodically, identifying the majority of backtracking/cross-movement/congestion points, with basic mitigations (signage, marked lanes) in place.
score_4_desc: The flow map is reviewed and updated on a defined cadence (e.g., quarterly) using actual movement/congestion data, with mitigations tracked and measurably reducing backtracking incidents year-on-year.
score_5_desc: The flow map is continuously validated against real operational data, with backtracking, cross-movement, and MHE/pedestrian conflict held at or near a documented practical minimum, reviewed as a standing facility-governance item.
indicative_scoring_questions:
• Does a current process-flow map of the facility exist, or is the last one outdated and never revisited?
• Does it identify backtracking, cross-movement between raw and processed material, and MHE/pedestrian conflict points?
• Is the map reviewed and updated on a defined cadence using actual movement/congestion data?
• Are mitigations (signage, marked lanes) in place, and is backtracking incidence trending down year-on-year?

score_1_desc:
None of the facility's ~18 functional zones (unloading, palletization, Sorting & Grading (S&G), S&G-staging-for-packing, packing, staging-for-picking-and-allocation, allocation, dispatch, ambient storage, chilled storage, leafy-processing, Material Handling Equipment (MHE) charging-and-staging, office, canteen, toilets, security, server room, electrical room) has a documented capacity/inventory math check.
Zone sizes are eyeballed.
Congestion, overflow, or significant underuse in one or more zones is common and unquantified.
Emergency-exit count and nearest-distance-to-exit adequacy never assessed as a design criterion.
Fire-extinguisher placement adequacy never assessed as a design criterion.
score_2_desc:
A handful of the ~18 zones (e.g., cold rooms) have an informal capacity sense.
Most zones have never had a capacity/inventory math check run against them.
Congestion/overflow incidents not logged by zone.
Emergency-exit count/distance and fire-extinguisher placement noted informally at best, not assessed as a design criterion.
score_3_desc:
The majority of the ~18 functional zones have been through a documented capacity/inventory math check (size derived from expected volume/inventory, not eyeballed), reviewed periodically.
Congestion/overflow incidents logged by zone.
Emergency-exit count and nearest-distance-to-exit adequacy assessed as a design criterion for majority of the facility.
Fire-extinguisher placement adequacy assessed as a design criterion, though not comprehensively across all zones.
score_4_desc:
All ~18 functional zones assessed on a defined cadence via a documented capacity/inventory math check.
Constrained zones flagged for a follow-up sizing study; excess-capacity zones flagged for reallocation.
Emergency-exit count and nearest-distance-to-exit adequacy assessed for the full facility, gaps tracked to closure.
Fire-extinguisher placement adequacy assessed for the full facility, gaps tracked to closure.
score_5_desc:
All ~18 functional zones continuously monitored against actual utilization data via a standing capacity/inventory math check.
Findings feed a facility-improvement backlog with measurable resolution of previously constrained zones.
Emergency-exit count and nearest-distance-to-exit adequacy fully assessed by design, zero unresolved gaps.
Fire-extinguisher placement adequacy fully assessed by design, zero unresolved coverage gaps.
indicative_scoring_questions:
• How many of the ~18 functional zones (unloading, palletization, Sorting & Grading (S&G), packing, staging, ambient/chilled storage, leafy processing, MHE charging, office, canteen, toilets, security, server room, electrical room) have a documented capacity/inventory math check, versus eyeballed sizing?
• Are congestion, overflow, or underuse incidents logged by zone?
• Has emergency-exit count and nearest-distance-to-exit adequacy been assessed as a design criterion, and across what % of the facility?
• Has fire-extinguisher placement adequacy been assessed as a design criterion?
• Are constrained zones flagged for a sizing study, and excess-capacity zones flagged for reallocation?

score_1_desc: Storage locations are assigned with no defined method (first-available-space); there is no concept of velocity-based ("golden zone") slotting; storage density and rack/bin utilization are not measured.
score_2_desc: A slotting concept exists informally for a handful of high-velocity SKUs, but is not documented or systematically applied; storage density is not measured.
score_3_desc: A documented slotting methodology (velocity-based, golden-zone placement) is applied to the majority of SKUs, with storage density/rack utilization measured periodically.
score_4_desc: Slotting is applied to over 90% of SKUs and reviewed on a defined cadence (e.g., monthly) using actual movement data; storage density and rack/bin utilization are tracked and held above a defined benchmark.
score_5_desc: Slotting is continuously optimized using real movement data for 100% of SKUs, with storage density/utilization tracked in real time and a documented, sustained improvement trend.
indicative_scoring_questions:
• Are storage locations assigned by a documented, velocity-based ("golden zone") slotting methodology, or first-available-space?
• What % of SKUs are covered by a documented slotting rule?
• Is storage density/rack-bin utilization measured, and how often?
• Is slotting re-optimized using actual movement data, with a documented improvement trend?

score_1_desc: There is no documented basis for whether the current number of docks is adequate for inbound/outbound volume; inbound and outbound share docks with no defined segregation, and queuing is chronic and unmeasured.
score_2_desc: Dock count feels adequate or inadequate based on staff perception only; queuing is noticed but not measured; inbound/outbound segregation is informal.
score_3_desc: Dock count and utilization are documented against average daily volume, reviewed periodically; a basic inbound/outbound segregation exists and is followed most of the time.
score_4_desc: Dock count and utilization are reviewed against both average and peak volume, with queuing time tracked and held under a defined target; inbound/outbound segregation is enforced with defined exceptions.
score_5_desc: Dock adequacy is continuously validated against actual and forecast peak volume, with queuing time consistently under target, zero unmanaged inbound/outbound conflicts, and dock-vehicle compatibility (size/type) planned for.
indicative_scoring_questions:
• Is dock count/utilization documented against average and peak daily volume, or judged on staff perception only?
• Is queuing time measured, and held under a defined target?
• Is inbound/outbound dock segregation formally defined and enforced, or informal?
• Is dock-vehicle compatibility (size/type) planned for?

score_1_desc: Cold-room civil condition (insulation integrity, door condition, ante-room presence, temperature uniformity across the room) has never been formally assessed; overloading beyond rated capacity is common and unmeasured.
score_2_desc: Civil condition is assessed only reactively (e.g., after a visible failure); ante-rooms, where absent, are not flagged as a design gap.
score_3_desc: A documented assessment of insulation, door condition, ante-room presence, and temperature uniformity exists for the majority of cold rooms, reviewed periodically; overloading incidents are logged.
score_4_desc: The assessment is refreshed on a defined cadence for all cold rooms, with identified gaps (missing ante-room, poor uniformity, overloading) tracked to resolution or flagged for a design study.
score_5_desc: Cold-room civil condition is continuously monitored (e.g., uniformity mapping) with zero unresolved insulation/door/ante-room gaps and utilization consistently within rated capacity.
indicative_scoring_questions:
• Has cold-room civil condition (insulation integrity, door condition, ante-room presence, temperature uniformity) been formally assessed, or only reactively after a failure?
• Where ante-rooms are absent, is that flagged as a design gap?
• Is overloading beyond rated capacity tracked, and how common is it?
• Are identified gaps (insulation, door, ante-room, uniformity) tracked to resolution or flagged for a design study?

score_1_desc: Raw and processed material flows are not physically segregated; personnel movement between zones is unrestricted; drainage, pest control, and wash-area provisions have not been assessed against a defined food-safety standard.
score_2_desc: Some segregation exists informally (e.g., separate tables) but personnel flow, drainage, and pest control are not assessed as a combined food-safety facility standard.
score_3_desc: A documented food-safety facility assessment (raw/processed segregation, personnel flow, drainage, pest control, wash/hand-wash areas) exists and is followed for the majority of the facility, reviewed periodically.
score_4_desc: The assessment is refreshed on a defined cadence (e.g., quarterly) with over 90% compliance against the defined standard, and identified gaps tracked to closure.
score_5_desc: Food-safety facility compliance is continuously monitored and audited, with zero unresolved gaps sustained across consecutive audit cycles, and cross-contamination risk points eliminated or fully controlled.
indicative_scoring_questions:
• Are raw and processed material flows physically segregated, and is personnel movement between zones restricted?
• Have drainage, pest control, and wash/hand-wash area provisions been assessed against a defined food-safety standard?
• Is there a documented food-safety facility assessment, and what % compliance does it show?
• Is the assessment refreshed on a defined cadence, with gaps tracked to closure?

score_1_desc: New employees start work with no formal induction; whatever orientation happens is informal, given by a co-worker, and not documented; there is no defined induction checklist or duration.
score_2_desc: A basic induction exists (e.g., a half-day safety/rules briefing) but is applied inconsistently and not tracked per new hire.
score_3_desc: A defined induction program (covering safety, quality/food-safety basics, role overview) exists and is completed by the majority of new hires before independent work begins, tracked via a checklist.
score_4_desc: The induction program is completed by over 90% of new hires, tracked systematically, with a basic competency check before sign-off to independent work.
score_5_desc: The induction program is completed by 100% of new hires with a documented competency sign-off, refreshed periodically for content relevance, and tracked as a standing Human Resources (HR)/Operations Key Performance Indicator (KPI).
indicative_scoring_questions:
• Is there a formal, documented induction checklist and duration for new hires, or is orientation informal and given by a co-worker?
• What % of new hires complete the defined induction program before starting independent work?
• Does induction cover safety, quality/food-safety basics, and role overview?
• Is there a competency check/sign-off before release to independent work?
• Is induction completion tracked as a standing Human Resources (HR)/Operations Key Performance Indicator (KPI)?

score_1_desc: There is no defined skill/Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) training curriculum per role; employees learn the job by observing peers, with no certification or sign-off.
score_2_desc: A training curriculum exists for some roles (e.g., QC, cold-chain handling) but not others; completion is not tracked or certified.
score_3_desc: A defined curriculum exists for the majority of roles, with completion tracked via a checklist or basic test for the majority of employees.
score_4_desc: The curriculum covers over 90% of roles with a formal certification/sign-off, tracked systematically, and refreshed when SOPs change.
score_5_desc: The curriculum covers 100% of roles with formal certification, systematically tracked, and directly linked to task authorization (e.g., an employee cannot be rostered to a task without current certification).
indicative_scoring_questions:
• Is there a defined skill/Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) training curriculum for each role, or do employees learn by observing peers?
• What % of roles have a defined curriculum, and what % of employees are certified against it?
• Is completion tracked via a checklist/test, or a formal certification/sign-off?
• Is certification refreshed when SOPs change, and is it linked to task authorization (can an uncertified employee still be rostered)?

score_1_desc:
Training effectiveness not measured at all.
No way to tell whether training improves on-the-job performance.
'Effective' training not tied to certification status - certification, where it exists, is untracked.
score_2_desc:
Training completion tracked (a headcount/attendance metric).
Effect on performance (productivity, error rate, quality) not measured.
Whether staff hold a valid role certification, or recertified on time, not linked to any effectiveness measure.
score_3_desc:
Time-to-target-productivity measured informally for some roles.
Productivity/error-rate comparisons between trained and untrained staff made occasionally, not routinely.
Effectiveness reviews for some roles note current certification status, but do not check recertification timeliness (tracked separately under the refresher/recertification-cadence subpoint).
score_4_desc:
Time-to-target-productivity and error-rate differential (trained vs. new) tracked routinely for majority of roles.
Feeds periodic curriculum updates.
'Effective' training for majority of roles requires a valid, current role certification - not just having attended training once.
Recertification timeliness (per the separate recertification-cadence subpoint) factored into the effectiveness view.
score_5_desc:
Training effectiveness tracked as a standing output metric for all roles (time-to-target-productivity, post-training error/productivity trend).
Curriculum continuously revised based on this data.
'Effective' training defined for 100% of roles as certified AND currently recertified.
An employee whose certification has lapsed is not counted as effectively trained, regardless of past performance - fully aligned with the recertification-cadence tracking elsewhere in this Knowledge Base.
indicative_scoring_questions:
• Is training effectiveness measured beyond attendance/headcount - e.g., time-to-target-productivity, or error-rate differential between trained and untrained staff?
• Is "effective" training tied to holding a valid, current role certification, or just having attended training once?
• Is recertification timeliness factored into whether someone counts as effectively trained?
• Does this effectiveness data feed periodic curriculum updates?

score_1_desc: Employees are trained and deployed in a single role only; there is no visibility into which roles have no backup-trained coverage; absenteeism in a critical role causes an immediate operational gap.
score_2_desc: Cross-training happens informally and opportunistically for a few individuals, not tracked as a coverage metric.
score_3_desc: A cross-training plan exists for the majority of critical roles, with coverage tracked periodically; single-point-of-failure roles are identified but not systematically closed.
score_4_desc: Cross-training coverage is tracked for over 90% of critical roles, with a defined target (e.g., at least 2 backup-trained employees per critical role) actively managed.
score_5_desc: Multi-skilling coverage is tracked in real time against a defined target for all critical roles, with zero unaddressed single-point-of-failure roles, sustained through routine roster planning.
indicative_scoring_questions:
• Are employees trained/deployed in a single role only, or is there a cross-training plan for critical roles?
• What % of critical roles have tracked backup coverage, and is there a defined target (e.g., at least 2 backup-trained employees per critical role)?
• Are single-point-of-failure roles identified, and are they being systematically closed?
• Does absenteeism in a critical role cause an immediate operational gap?

subpoint_name: Continuous Improvement Culture & Frontline Idea Generation
score_1_desc: There is no mechanism for frontline employees to submit improvement ideas; continuous improvement, where it happens, is driven exclusively top-down by management or external consultants.
score_2_desc: A suggestion box or informal channel exists but ideas are rarely reviewed or acted upon; there is no tracking of submission or implementation.
score_3_desc: A defined idea-submission mechanism exists and is reviewed periodically (e.g., monthly), with implemented ideas tracked, though participation is limited to a small group of employees.
score_4_desc: The mechanism is actively promoted with participation from the majority of teams, ideas are reviewed on a defined cadence with feedback given to submitters, and implementation rate is tracked.
score_5_desc: A sustained continuous-improvement culture exists with broad frontline participation, a fast review-and-feedback cycle, recognition for implemented ideas, and a tracked, positive trend in submission/implementation rate over time.
indicative_scoring_questions:
• Is there a mechanism for frontline employees to submit improvement ideas, and is it actually reviewed?
• What share of teams/employees participate - broad, or limited to a small group?
• Are submitted ideas tracked through to implementation, with feedback given to submitters?
• Is there recognition for implemented ideas, and a tracked trend in submission/implementation rate over time?

score_1_desc: There is no refresher or recertification cadence for any role; training is a one-time event at hiring, with skills/knowledge assumed to persist indefinitely (including for food-safety and safety-critical roles).
score_2_desc: Refreshers happen occasionally and informally (e.g., after an incident) but are not scheduled or tracked.
score_3_desc: A defined refresher cadence exists for the majority of safety-critical and food-safety roles, tracked via a checklist, though adherence to the schedule is inconsistent.
score_4_desc: The refresher cadence covers over 90% of applicable roles with tracked adherence, and content is updated when SOPs or regulations change.
score_5_desc: The refresher/recertification cadence covers 100% of applicable roles, is systematically tracked with automated due-date reminders, and compliance is sustained at a defined benchmark (e.g., 98%+) across consecutive cycles.
indicative_scoring_questions:
• Is there a defined refresher/recertification cadence for safety-critical and food-safety roles, or is training a one-time event at hiring?
• What % of applicable roles/employees are covered by the cadence, and what is current recertification compliance %?
• Are refreshers scheduled and tracked, or only triggered informally after an incident?
• Is content updated when SOPs or regulations change, with automated due-date reminders in place?
